# ON THE SIGNATURE OF ALL THINGS,
### or
## Of the Birth and Designation of All Beings.

### Preface of the Author
#### to the Wisdom-loving Reader.

For the human being, whom God has created in his image and likeness, there is nothing more useful in all the labors he pursues than to constantly contemplate what he is: (2) from whence good and evil come to him, (3) and how he leads himself into evil and good. In such contemplation (4) he may also find and learn the <term>Cure<note>original: "Curam." Refers to both the medical treatment of the body and the spiritual care/healing of the soul.</note></term> for body and soul; and (5) how he should prepare himself so that salvation in body and soul may be introduced and opened within him. He also learns (6) through such contemplation to know his Creator, and (7) the mysteries of the great wonders of God become known and manifest to him. This not only awakens a knowledge of the great wonders of God within the person, but also (8) a heartfelt desire and refuge in the love and grace of God; in which desire the image of God becomes manifest to him (9) within himself through the <term>Will-spirit<note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Will-spirit" is the active force of human intent that directs the soul's desire toward either God or the self.</note></term>—which travels in desire toward God himself—just as God has manifested himself in his eternal desire with the essence that <term>originated<note>original: "geurständet." A specialized term used by Böhme to describe something coming into primordial existence or "standing forth" out of the divine source.</note></term> in that desire through his own Spirit.

2. Since God then created man as a likeness of Himself out of his eternal and temporal essence, and ordained him as lord and ruler of his creation, and also put all things under his feet: this did not happen to the end that he should be as an irrational beast. Rather, he shall learn to rightly recognize the wonders of God in his creation, and the great God in his threefold, unified essence, so that he may know how to maintain his life and conduct himself before God in this office on Earth which has been commanded to him,

<summary>In this preface, Jacob Böhme introduces the necessity of self-knowledge, arguing that by understanding one's own nature as an image of God, a person can find the "cure" for body and soul and recognize the divine signature in all of creation.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Signature of All Things, image of God, self-contemplation, Cure of the soul, Will-spirit, divine wonders, anthropology, spiritual healing</keywords>

...shall, so that he may attain temporal and eternal salvation, and the inheritance for which God created him.

3. From such contemplation, I have now resolved to write down these mysteries—which the Spirit of God reveals to the person who applies themselves with genuine earnestness—and to lead them, as if in a <term>Love-play<note>original: "Liebe-Spiel." A mystical concept in which the interaction between God and the soul is seen as a joyful, non-coercive, and harmonious "play" of divine forces.</note></term> of his wonders. My goal is to give the (loving), God-fearing reader and seeker of God's wisdom a cause to be moved and filled with desire, even a hunger, for the <term>Little Pearl<note>original: "Perlein." A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" from the Gospel parables, representing the discovery of the divine spark or Wisdom (Sophia) within the soul.</note></term>, which is more precious than the outward world. Through this: (1) the wonders of God may be revealed in us, (2) his holy name may be praised and recognized in and by us, (3) and Satan’s kingdom may also be exposed and hindered. Furthermore, (4) that the human being might learn to recognize God’s will toward them, and depart from the entirely useless and erroneous strife from which brotherly disunity arises. Thus, the loving will of God toward us—which is currently dragged into pure conflict—might be recognized and made manifest; for such strife is a void and highly damaging thing that does not <term>originate<note>original: "urstände." A specialized term used by Böhme to describe something coming into primordial existence or "standing forth" out of its source.</note></term> in God’s will, but in the will and desire of the Devil. From this strife, the noble image of God rightly departs, entering instead into the true knowledge of God, his will, and his essence.

4. Although Reason cries out: "Bring forth the Scriptures and the letters!", the external letter alone is not enough for true knowledge, even though it serves as the guide to the foundation. The <term>Living Letter<note>original: "lebendige Buchstabe." Böhme contrasts the "dead" external text of religious law with the active, speaking presence of God's Word within the human spirit.</note></term>—which is God's own self-subsisting, spoken Word and essence—must also be opened and read within the person themselves, guided by the spoken Word, wherein the Holy Spirit is the reader and the revealer. Therefore, my intention is to write down the true foundation of all beings, according to my knowledge and gifts, just as the Spirit of understanding has opened it within me, and to keep it as a brief <term>Memorial<note>original: "Memorial." Used here in the sense of a foundational remembrance or a spiritual handbook for practice.</note></term> and exercise, so that if anyone should desire to search further, they might find and experience such benefit within themselves.

5. However, it is not my intention to lead people into misunderstood or useless arts for which they are neither called nor gifted by God; for I myself do not...

## Chapter 1.
### How all things spoken of God are mute and without understanding without the knowledge of the Signature; and how the Signature lies within the human mind according to the Being of all beings.

->Summaries.<-

Everything spoken of God without the knowledge of the Signature is mute. §. 1. The resonance and Spirit must enter from its signature into mine and designate its form within my own; 2. for everything comes from one root, 3. and a like sound catches and moves the other. 4. The Signature is a container of the spirit, 5. and lies most artfully within the human <term>mind<note>original: "Gemüth." This term encompasses the mind, soul, and emotional disposition of a person.</note></term>. 6. The human being contains the forms of all three worlds within themselves; 7. whichever world is primary, that one forms the person. 8. Although one <term>Fiat<note>Latin: "Let it be." Referring to the creative Word of God that brings things into existence.</note></term> may halt another, 9. 10. and the will can be broken by one that is stronger. 11. A person is known by their daily practice: 12. so too animals and herbs have their outward character, 13. 14. as the internal always works toward its own revelation. 15. Therefore, the greatest understanding is found in the Signature, 16. as is the <term>Language of Nature<note>original: "Natur-Sprache." The idea that the true names of things correspond perfectly to their inner essences, a language lost after the Fall.</note></term>. 17.

Everything that is spoken, written, or taught about God without the knowledge of the Signature is mute and without understanding; for it originates only from a historical delusion, from another...

The specific inherent quality or character of a thing.</term>, it does not easily let its innate form be noticed—unless that form be provoked, in which case it breaks forth before all other forms.

So it is also with the herbs of the earth; if an herb is moved from a poor field into a good one, it immediately acquires a stronger body, as well as a lovelier scent and power, and thus manifests its inner **essence**<term>original: *Eſſenz*. The spiritual substance or core qualities.</term> in its outward appearance.

15. And there is no thing in nature, created or born, that does not manifest its inner form outwardly as well; for the internal is constantly working toward revelation. We recognize this in the power and the **configuration**<term>original: *Geſtaltniß*. The internal spiritual shaping or tuning of a thing's character.</term> of this world, seeing how the eternal Being, through its outward-birthing in desire, has revealed itself in a likeness—revealing itself in as many forms and shapes as we see and recognize in the stars and elements, as well as in the creatures, trees, and herbs.

16. Therefore, the greatest understanding lies in the **signature**<term>original: *Signatur*. The "signature" is the outward mark or form that reveals the hidden inner spirit and purpose of any created thing.</term>. Within this, a person (as the image of the greatest virtue) not only learns to know themselves, but may also learn to recognize the **Being of all beings**<note>original: *Weſen aller Weſen*. Böhme’s term for the ultimate source or God, from whom all individual beings derive.</note>. For by the outward configuration of all creatures—by their drive and desire, and likewise by their outgoing resonance, voice, and language—one recognizes the hidden spirit. For nature has given every thing its own language according to its essence and form. From the essence, the language or resonance **originates**<term>original: *urſtändet*. A term Böhme uses to describe the essential "standing up" or arising of a thing from its source.</term>; and the **Fiat**<note>original: *Fiat*. Latin for "Let it be." The creative word or force that gives form to an object's qualities.</note> of that same essence shapes the quality of the essence into the outgoing resonance or power: the living quality in the resonance, and the essential quality in the scent, power, and form. Every thing has its mouth for revelation.

17. And that is the **language of nature**<note>original: *Natur-Sprache*. The idea that all things "speak" their true nature through their physical properties and sounds.</note>, through which every thing speaks from its own property and always manifests and represents itself, showing what it is good and useful for. For every thing reveals its "mother," who provides the essence and the will for its form in this way.

## The 2nd Chapter.
# Of the Conflict and Strife in the Essence of All Beings.

->Summaries.<-

From the many wills come strife and sickness, as well as medicine. §. 1. 2. The physician stands in equality <note>original: *Gleichheit*. Refers to a state of balance or harmony</note>, 3. whereas, conversely, nature is made manifest in strife. 4. How to advise regarding this conflict? 5. Human life stands in three principles and has a twofold spirit. 6. Eternal nature originates in desire; from this comes darkness: 7. and from the darkness, the other will goes out and enters into itself; 8. thereby creating three forms, namely: Harshness, Drawing, and Anxiety <note>original: *Herbe, Ziehen und Angst*. These are the first three "properties" of nature in Böhme’s system</note>, through which wrath arises, 9. 10. and also where enmity originates. 11. The free will is *Sul* <note>original: *Sul*. Böhme interprets this as the soul or light-principle</note>, and *Phur* <note>original: *Phur*. Interpreted as the fire or desire-principle</note> is the desire, in which the origin of eternal and outward nature is understood, 12. and it creates a dark fire-world and a light fire-world. 13. Torment is the physician of free delight: just as light is the physician of dark nature, 14. 15. so that love and anger dwell within one another, and one is the physician of the other through the **imagination** <term>original: *Imagination*. Not merely fantasy, but the formative power of the spirit to "image" or shape reality.</term>. 16. The second form in nature is the "Wheel," and in the third principle, it is called **Mercury** <term>original: *Mercurius*. The principle of movement, communication, and sound.</term>. 17. It is the form of restlessness and seeks rest: it has a twofold desire and two wills. 18. 19. Two physicians. 20. The third will is the spirit, a master of wrath and love. 21. As the instrument is struck, so is the sound. 22. The desire for freedom is called **God**, and the desire toward nature is called **God’s wrath**. 23. The third form is Anxiety, which with the other forms makes the fire, and in the third principle is called **Salt** <term>original: *Saltz*. The principle of physical substance, contraction, and preservation.</term>; 24. it has both a cold and a hot fire within it. 25. These three forms are one and also have one mother. 26. Anxiety also has two wills within it. 27. The will, with its desire, creates the **center of nature** <note>original: *Centrum Naturæ*</note>. 28. With the center within itself, the dark world is understood; and from it, the outward world. 29. The desire of the dark world is for revelation, 30. and the desire of the outward world is **Sulphur**, **Mercury**, and **Salt**. 31. How thunder and lightning are born? 32. etc.

Since there are so many and varied forms, and each produces another will from its own **property** <term>original: *Eigenſchaft*. The specific inherent quality or character of a being.</term> that differs from the others, we understand herein the conflict and the strife in the **essence of all beings** <note>original: *Wesen aller Wesen*</note>. We see how each thing is hostile to, poisons, and kills the other—that is, it overcomes the other's essence and the spirit of that essence, leading it into another form. From this, sickness and pain arise when one essence breaks another.

7. We understand that outside of nature there is an eternal stillness and rest, which is the **Nothing**; and then we understand that in the eternal **Nothing** an eternal **Will** originates, to lead the **Nothing** into **Something**, so that the **Will** may find, feel, and behold itself. For in the **Nothing**, the **Will** would not be manifest to itself; thus we recognize that the **Will** seeks itself, and finds itself within itself. Its seeking is a **Desire**, and its finding is the **Essence** <note>original: *Wesen*. In Böhme's thought, this refers to both "being" and "substance"—the "stuff" of reality.</note> of the **Desire**, within which the **Will** finds itself. It finds nothing but the quality of **Hunger**, which it is itself; it draws this into itself—that is, it draws itself into itself—and finds itself within itself. This drawing-into-itself creates a shadowing or **Darkness** within the **Will**, which does not exist in **Freedom** <note>original: *Freyheit*. Refers to the "Unground" or the absolute liberty of the divine before creation.</note> (as in the **Nothing**); for the **Will** of **Freedom** shadows itself with the **Essence** of **Desire**, because it is the **Desire** that creates **Essence**, and not the **Will**.

8. Yet it cannot reach the **Freedom** outside of itself, for the **Desire** goes out from itself and creates torment and **Darkness**. Thus the **Will** (understand: the second created **Will**) must go within itself—and yet there is no separation. For within itself, before the **Desire**, lies **Freedom** as the **Nothing**. Yet the **Will** cannot be a **Nothing**, for it desires to reveal itself within the **Nothing**; and yet no **Revelation** can happen except through the **Essence** of the **Desire**. The more the recaptured **Will** desires **Revelation**, the more and the more severely the **Desire** draws into itself, creating within itself three **Forms** <note>original: *Gestalten*. These are the first three of Böhme's Seven Qualities of Nature.</note>.

9. These are: first, the **Desire**, which is **Harshness** <term>original: *Herbe*. Also translated as "Astringency." The "pulling" or "drawing" creates a **Sting** <note>original: *Stachel*. A prickling or stimulus.</note> or **Movement** within the **Hardness**, a state of enmity against the harsh, indrawn **Hardness**. This pulling is the second **Form**, and it is the cause of **Motion** and **Life**; it stirs within the **Harshness** and **Hardness**, which the **Hardness** (as the enclosure) cannot tolerate, and therefore draws itself together much more vehemently to hold the **Sting**—

All of this takes its origin from the eternal Nothing.

20. The physician of the first will is the pleasure of freedom; if the will attains this, it becomes full of joy within itself. The physician and helper of the other will—the will of nature—is the wrath within the hungry desire. Here, one understands **God’s love and wrath**, and how evil and good exist in the center of every life, and how no joy may arise without sorrow, and how one is the physician to the other.

# Chapter 3. And the Signification of All Beings.

...is the water <note>This completes the thought from the previous page regarding the "indestructible essence" arising from eternal nature.</note> of which Christ tells us, that He wishes to give us to drink, and whoever should drink of the same, it would well up in him into a spring of eternal life; John 4:14. In the shock of the bursting <note>original: *Schracke des Zersprengens*; Böhme refers to a spiritual-chemical reaction where the divine light breaks through the darkness of "nature" to create life.</note>, it also retains the fiery property which is called Heaven, in which the wonders of the Divine Kingdom of Joy are known and revealed; and in the watery property it is the Greening or Paradise. For in the fiery property, the eternal element arises, which is the true essence of the Divine Corporeality <term>Divine Corporeality: Böhme's idea that God is not just a formless spirit, but possesses a spiritual "body" or substance from which the universe is made</term>, within which everything stands that may be known in God, as has been sufficiently explained in our other writings on Divine Revelation in an orderly progression, concerning Divine Wisdom and the Divine, eternal, bottomless birth. Now we turn to the essence of the external world: to the revelation of the Eternal in the form of metals, herbs, and trees, as well as humans and animals.

31. We see that the metals have a different body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> than the living creatures, or than the earth and stones; so Reason asks what the origin <note>original: *Urstand*</note> of each thing might be, since in the beginning everything arose from One Mother, and yet eternity has no temporal beginning? There we must once again consider the Mother of the first birth-giver, and see how and in what way one essence separates from the other: how the beginning-bound separates from the Eternal, and time from eternity; and yet one stands within the other, but separates into two Principles, namely into God’s Kingdom and the kingdom of this world—and yet all is God’s.

32. But because Christ calls the Devil a Prince of this world, John 12:31, we can also say in what he is a prince; we can also say that this world is not his property, and that he is the poorest creature in this world. So look upon the first ground, upon the Mother who has given birth to all creatures, as well as the earth, stones, and all metals; her property stands in spiritual Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, these are the three qualities of all existence: Sulphur (the soul/fire), Mercury (the spirit/movement), and Salt (the body/solidity).</note>, and everything that has begun arose in and out of her Impression <note>original: *Impression*; refers to the spiritual "thickening" or "contraction" of desire into physical matter.</note>. Initially, it entered into a creaturely form through the Mother’s first quality—the harsh drawing-into-itself—by way of the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done"; the divine command of creation.</note>, and it yields a manifold essence and spirit according to the primary property of the Separation <note>original: *Scheidung*; the process by which the unified divine light differentiates into the diverse forms of the natural world.</note>.

### Chapter 3 and the Designation of All Beings

...[exists], and is the same anxious being as that which originates from Desire. Instead, they pass together through the ignition of the fire, through the Salnitrous Crack <term>Salnitrischer Schrack: A key term for Böhme, referring to a sudden, explosive "crack" or "fright" like the ignition of gunpowder (saltpeter), marking the moment when the dark, tense forces of nature are transformed into light.</term>. Thus the spirit, as the torment, becomes material (by which is meant the very sharp, fiery torment of anxiety) and retains only an essential working, like a powerless desire. In the ignition of the fire within the Salnitrous Crack, every property separates within itself, and the entire material substance becomes a particular thing, such as metals, stones, and earths.

39. However, because Freedom is captured within it along with the *Sul* <note>original: *Sul*; Böhme often divides the word "Sulphur" into *Sul* (the light or oil of the soul) and *Phur* (the burning fire).</note> or light-property, the *Sul* presses outward to reveal itself, just as is the nature of Freedom's Delight. From this it follows that metals grow, whereas the coarse, hard stones do not; the stones were captured too harshly in the compression out of the wrathful essence and have too little *Sul* within them. But as for the precious stones with their brilliance and great virtue <note>In historical science, "virtue" refers to a substance's inherent power or medicinal property.</note>, they have their origin in the Flash of the Fire <note>original: *Blize des Feuers*</note> where death and life separate. Since one part sinks down because of the dark essence and the other rises up because of Freedom—and yet everything is brought into substantiality within the "crack"—that same glance or flash also becomes material. This is why they are hard and shimmering <note>original: *schielicht*; literally "squinting," but here describing the way light plays in a gemstone or an eye.</note> like an eye; for the origin of the eye or of the shine within the body is also like this when life is ignited, all according to the Law of Eternity. And for this reason, they possess such great power and virtue that they are very near to the Godhead and carry within them the embodied name of the Divine Power; just as gold also [partakes] of the Divine...

# XIV. Concerning the Birth: Chapter 3

...essence or heavenly corporeality is near; so that if one were to dissolve the dead body and make of it a flying, weaving spirit—which can only happen through God’s movement—then one would see what it truly would be. 40. Furthermore, we must also consider the other metals and minerals, which likewise take their origin in this way. However, in the Salnitric Crack <term>Salnitrischer Schrack: A term used by Böhme to describe a sudden, explosive "fright" or ignition—like saltpeter catching fire—where spiritual forces suddenly crystallize into material properties.</term>, every property separates itself. We see this in how the properties of fire and light are of many kinds, and all of this comes from the first "impression" or contraction. Before that contraction, the Delight of Freedom and the Desire stood within one another like a Chaos—a vision of great wonders, where all colors, power, and virtues lie in this single Chaos or Miracle-Eye. This Chaos is God Himself, as the Being of all beings, who thus reveals Himself in particularity through the Eye of Eternity. Every material substance is a being according to the spirit from which it was born; and if one ignites it in the fire, it yields such a light as the spirit is within the essence.

41. Thus we must also think of the metals: whatever kind of spirit is in each, it has a corresponding luster and also a corresponding body. Just as the Mind <note>original: *Gemüthe*; the deep, underlying seat of the soul's will and emotions.</note> swings the senses from the highest to the lowest, and grasps the lowest up to the highest through the senses; so also has the Eternal Mind revealed itself from the highest Majesty down into the very lowest—even into the greatest darkness. This world with its sun, stars, and elements, together with every created being, is nothing other than a revelation of eternity, of the eternal Will and Mind. And just as it came to be in the beginning, so it still stands in its simmering <note>original: *Sud*; literally a "brew" or "boiling," implying that creation is an ongoing alchemical process of growth.</note> and growth; it still drives toward light and darkness, toward evil and good. Everything stands in these first three forms: in Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt <term>Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt: In Böhme’s alchemy, these are not just chemicals but the "Tria Prima"—the three fundamental spiritual forces that make up all physical matter.</term>, one degree after another.

42. For in this way also are the choirs of spirits, likewise the stars, the trees, the herbs, and all lineages of whatever has ever come to be, as well as the inner, heavenly choirs with their distinctions.

The sixth form arises from the turning wheel before the fire, where the multiplication of the essence arises from the property of *Mercury* <note>original: *Mercurius*; in theosophical alchemy, this represents the principle of movement, sound, and the "word" or communication.</note>, in the nitrous shock <note>original: *salnitrisch*; refers to the explosive, lightning-like spiritual force associated with saltpeter or "niter."</note>. With the ignition of the fire, one form is led into the other; so now, as the love-desire penetrates through all forms, all forms become entirely desiring, one after another, for the love-child (as *Venus* <note>original: *Venus*; the property of love, sweetness, and outward beauty.</note>) is in them all.

11. Here begin taste, smell, hearing, seeing, and feeling, as well as speaking: for the light unlocks another principle <note>original: *Principium*; a fundamental realm or state of being.</note> of another quality and fills everything; there life greens in death, as love in wrath, and the light shines in the darkness. Here the Bridegroom embraces his Bride, and **God** himself resists his own wrath, as the fierceness of nature. And in this form arises all speech, understanding, and the senses, and the true real life of all creatures, as well as in growing things, like trees and herbs, in each thing according to its property.

12. The seventh form arises from all the others and is the others' body, dwelling-house, or food; for this happens thus: When the other forms, in penetrating one another...

<header>XIV. On the Birth Ch. 4.</header>

...taste one another in the love-desire, then in every form there arises a hunger or desire for love, as for the light; thus every hunger is outgoing toward the thing it desires, and then firmly drawing the property of the desired thing into itself. Thus, one essence is formed from the two—namely, from the hunger and from that which the hunger desires. For this hunger does not stand in death; it no longer shuts itself into death, unless it be far too great, such that the imagination <note>original: *Einbildung*; for Böhme, this is not just "fantasy" but the literal "in-ward forming" of a desire into a reality.</note> in the hunger is too great. And then, if the hunger cannot reach that same thing, it suffocates, just as a child sometimes suffocates in the mother’s womb when this form is ignited in another form to eat of an external thing, for which the mother is thus ignited in lust; and if she does not receive it, the child cannot receive it either; now it suffocates in hunger, or a limb is ruined from which that hunger originated.

13. The first hunger in the center <term>Center: original *Centro*; the inward point of origin for spiritual forces.</term> before the fire is a spiritual hunger; it creates the **Dark-World**, and the hunger of free delight creates the **Light-World**. These are both only spirit until they pass through the ignition of the fire together; then they have died to the spirit and are a likeness of the first spirit, as a revelation of the ungraspable spirit, who is called **God** in love and wrath, in a two-fold source-torment <note>original: *Qual*; Böhme frequently puns on the similarity between *Qual* (torment) and *Quelle* (source/spring), implying that the "torment" of the fire is also the "source" of its life.</note>.

14. Thus each now stands within itself unseparated—as **God** in time, and time in **God**—and neither is the other, yet they come from one eternal origin. Thus the temporal spirit-hunger gives a temporal body, and the eternal spirit-hunger an eternal body; they are both within one another, and neither is the other.

15. The **seven forms** <term>Seven Forms: the foundational qualities of nature in Böhme's system, through which the divine manifests from stillness into physical existence.</term> make for themselves a body according to their hunger out of their own self-property; therefore, everything that the spirit has in all its properties lies within the body. Furthermore, we are to recognize that a distinction has indeed occurred in the creation of this world; for one sees this in the sun and stars, as well as in all creatures, also in metals, stones, and earths, for that same thing is the **Revelation of God**.

### Chapter 4. and the Designation of all Beings.

...are lesser minerals <note>original: *Mineralia minora*</note> (lesser ores), as are the stars; and just as the planetary wheel <term>Planetary wheel: The cyclical movement of the celestial bodies, which Böhme viewed as a cosmic clockwork or loom weaving the fabric of material reality.</term> has its internal state, so too is the birth of every thing.

17. The Godhead, as the Divine Light, is the center <note>original: *Centrum*</note> of all life; likewise in the revelation of God—as in the outward figure—the Sun is the center of all life. In the highest life, the highest things began, and then proceeded one out of the other down to the lowest; in every external thing there are two properties: one from **time**, the other from **eternity**. The first property, of time, is manifest [visible], and the other is hidden, yet it still presents a **likeness** of itself within every thing.

18. Whatever begins from the *desire of freedom* <note>The "desire of freedom" refers to the primordial longing of the divine "Nothing" (the *Ungrund*) to become "Something."</note> has its root in a heavenly property and its body in an earthly one; but the eternal stands within time, and reveals itself through time. **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*; for Böhme, this represents the soul-principle or the internal fire of growth.</note> is, in one part, heavenly within, and earthly according to its body; nevertheless, it brings forth a heavenly likeness from itself according to the Eternal, which is fixed and stable—as can be seen in **gold**. This is to be understood much more regarding the **Human Body**: if it had not been corrupted through desire in **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurio*; the principle of movement, vitality, and speech.</note>, then in Sulfur would stand the spiritual man (the heavenly one), and in Mercury the bodily man (the likeness of the Divine). Thus also is the metallic property in Sulfur the noblest and highest, for it is the highest spirit.

19. Understand it this way: in the heavenly realm, there is also the property of a **seething** <term>Seething: original *Sudes*; an alchemical metaphor for the intense, creative "boiling" or maturation of spiritual forces.</term> when freedom is seized and ignited in the highest desire, in which the realm of joy arises. This happens in the heavenly Sulfur, where it becomes an essence in the heavenly Mercury—that is, in the **Eternal Word**—which is a spiritual essence. But if this same spirituality longs to reveal itself in a likeness—both according to the spirit and the essence, according to the Trinity <note>original: *Dreyheit*</note> of the Godhead, and according to the mortal and immortal essence—then that same image is presented through the stars and the elements, and finally in **Man**, who is a living image of this entire essence, according to both the Divine and the outer world. The inner and outer worlds are also represented by the **metals** in a mortal image, as a likeness of the living, heavenly essence.

# XIV. On Birth, Chapter 4.

20. The beginning is in **Sulfur**; first, *Sul* is the delight of the light or of freedom, which longs for revelation and cannot occur except through fire. In the *Phur*, the desire arises as a severe contraction, which creates the dark, earthly property and the severity of the spirit as the fiery essence. In this severity, **Saturn** arises, which is the "compressed"; and **Mercury**, which is the "hunger of desire"; and the rager and breaker **Mars**, who is the wrath within that hunger, a cause of anger. These three belong to the *Phur*, acting as the property of desire for the free delight. <note>original: *Sulphur*. Böhme uses a mystical etymology here: "Sul" represents the sun or light (*Sol*), and "Phur" represents the fire (*Pyr*) or the driving, sometimes harsh, energetic force.</note>

21. The property of free delight gives birth to essence in the upper three forms—namely in Saturn, Mercury, and Mars—for it gives itself into every property. Thus, the property within the hunger of Mercury creates a bodily shape for it. However, since the free delight also becomes a "hunger" within that severe desiring, it also creates three forms after its own likeness: **Jupiter**, which is the origin of delight; **Venus**, which is the desire for delight; and **Luna** <note>The Moon</note>, which is the body of delight. And according to the property of light, it creates **Gold**. All of this is spirit. But now, in the hunger of every spirit, an essence also comes into being, according to the mortal and the immortal, a fixed and an unfixed, a figure according to the Heavenly and a figure according to the Earthly. <term>Fixed and Unfixed: In alchemy, "fixed" refers to substances that resist fire (like gold), while "unfixed" or "volatile" refers to those that evaporate or change (like mercury).</term>

22. In the Saturnine property, the desire of free delight—acting according to Saturn’s own property—creates **Lead**; according to the watery property within Saturn, it creates **Salt**; and according to the earthly, mortal property within Saturn, it creates stones and earth, and everything similar to them.

23. But according to "freedom"—or the free desire according to its own property—insofar as it yields itself to Saturn as the "desiring" force, it creates **Gold** within Saturn, according to the desire of the light. There, the spirit and the body part ways: the spirit of their desire is **Sol** <note>The Sun</note>, and the body is Gold. Understand this: the golden body is within Saturn according to the property of the free desire, and not according to Saturn's own property. His own property within himself is lead, salt, and earth, but he keeps the "golden child" locked inside himself like a **black raven**—not in his grey form, but in a dark glass. He is a great lord, but his lordship, on account of the golden child he carries in his belly, does not consist in his... <note>Böhme uses the "Black Raven" (*Corvus*) as an alchemical symbol for the *nigredo* or "blackness" stage, where the potential for gold is hidden within base, dark matter.</note>

Then it belongs in a foreign fire—and yet not foreign—which is an earnest fire. Thus the Father gives the soul as the fire-spirit; and its first mother (whom Mercury ate in his hunger, and who was fixed and perfect) gives the soul-spirit as the light-life. Then the Dead arises (this is the **Tincture**, which colors the body) and the child is born. Hereafter, it is its own master and a child of freedom, and it no longer asks anything of its master craftsman. It is better than its father, but not better than its mother, in whose seed it lay before the father worked within it. But silver has the property of neither Venus nor Mercury, for it retains the property of its mother—namely, Gentleness in Freedom—and is "hatched" just like gold. Because of the Sun, the Moon has a heavenly property; but because of its own form arising from the property of Desire, it possesses an almost earthly property. It is a sack and a vessel for both earthly and heavenly essence, much like the external body of man, which in **Adam** before the Fall was comparable to silver. But when he died to his [spiritual] delight, only the earthly property lived within him; therefore, he hungers forever after the radiance of the **Sun**. He would gladly shine again with the Moon from the Sun, but he only receives an earthly, lunar radiance, in which he practices pride—unless he is born again from the Sun’s radiance, that is, from **God’s power**, within the heavenly Mercury. ### 38 XIV. Concerning the Birth, Chapter 4.

32. From **Jupiter** <note>original: *Jove*</note> the wheel turns further; thus from the separation comes **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> with a broken metal, according to the property of his spirit: outwardly he is quicksilver, and inwardly he is a work of Paradise. In his spiritual property, he is the articulator of words, voices, and languages: It is written, God made all things through his Word; the heavenly, eternal Mercury is his Word, which the Father speaks forth in the kindling of his light, and that which is spoken is his **Wisdom** <note>original: *Weisheit*</note>, and the Word is the worker and maker of the formations within that spoken wisdom.

33. Now, whatever the inner Mercury does in God’s power within, the outer Mercury also does in the outer power, within the created being; he is God’s instrument, with which He works outwardly, toward death and toward life, in every thing according to its property. He builds up and he breaks down: according to the property of **Saturn**, he builds, and according to his own property, he distinguishes; he breaks the hardness in Saturn, acting as that which is enclosed, and opens it toward life. He opens the colors and creates shapes, and carries within himself both a heavenly and an earthly property. In the earthly property, he leads from the first desire toward nature—as out of Saturn comes **Mars**, the fierceness of the **Impression** <term>Impression: In Böhme's thought, this is the "drawing-in" or contraction of spiritual desire into a dense, material state</term>—for Mars is his soul, wherein Mercury lives. He gives to Mars the fiery essence, and stands under Jupiter in the order of the wheel, moving upward again; for he carries the fire-spirit in **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*</note>, in all planets and forms, and gives to every thing its **source-quality** <term>Qual: A technical term for Böhme, combining the meanings of "source" (Quelle), "quality" (Qualität), and "torment" or "labor" (Qual)</term> and the true spirit of life.

34. **Mars** is, in the first impression, the great anxiety, and causes the "will of love" of freedom to separate from him; that which is separated is called God, and the anxiety or the fire-source is called God’s wrath, as the fierceness of eternal nature. And just as God’s love in the interior separates from God’s wrath—that is, from the fierce property of eternal nature, like heaven from hell, or God from the devil—the same also happens in the external birth of nature.

### Chapter 4. and the Designation of All Beings.

35. ...lines beneath the **Sun** <note>original: *Sonnen*</note>, for such is the separation in nature, and thus one thing proceeds from another; her metal is **copper**, and the original state <note>original: *Urstand*</note> is this: that love is a desire, and yet desires only light and joy. For the **matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note> becomes a property out of the love-desire; but if the love-desire is to become bodily in the **Impression** <term>Impression: In Böhme's philosophy, this is the "drawing-in" or contraction of spirit that creates density and matter.</term>, it must yield itself to the fierce **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat*—Latin: "Let it be done," referring here to the creative word that hardens spirit into substance.</note>, acting as the desire of **Mars** in the fire or in the fiery property; for the **Saturnine** property takes everything into its power and makes it bodily.

36. Therefore, the metal of **Venus** is closely related to **gold**, because of its own property arising from freedom; but Mars makes it too fierce and too brittle, because it separates itself from Mars's fire, and so it retains a large portion of Mars's property within itself.

37. The metal of **Mars** is **iron**, for he is the fierceness in the **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: In the alchemy of this period, Sulphur represents the active, combustible, and soul-like principle of a substance.</term>, in which the fire kindles and originates. His origin with the matter is in the severity of the desire; copper separates itself from iron in the birth, for it originates from the will of Venus, and there is a distinction between them, as between body and soul. For Mars is the **fire-soul** of Venus and causes Venus to become bodily; otherwise, Venus, according to her own property in the deadening within the **nitrous terror** <note>original: *salnitrischen Schracke*—a term used to describe the explosive or flash-like transition of spiritual energy into matter.</note>, would yield only water. For her fire is merely a laughter or a love-fire—what she is alone without other influences; therefore, she cannot by her own power give birth to any bodily being that would be hard or tough. She is merely the woman to her child without a creaturely soul; Mars is her soul, and **Saturn** makes her body. The spirit of **Sol** <note>original: *Sol*—Latin for the Sun, representing the divine light-source.</note> may **tinge** <term>Tinge: To transform or transmute the inner nature of a substance, especially in an alchemical sense.</term> Mars and Venus and transform them into the highest metallic perfection, namely into gold, which cannot happen so easily with **silver** unless it is first brought back into the **first matter**, where Saturn, Mars, and Mercury are together in the Sulphur; then it may be so. Venus receives her toughness from Saturn and her redness from Mars, as from the fire.

38. Now, the desire of Venus is only intense for Sol, as for her first mother, from whom she springs in her birth in her first origin; for love springs from God: Thus it is also in the figure in the **out-birth** <note>original: *Ausgeburt*—the external, physical manifestation of an internal spiritual process.</note>.

## The 5th Chapter.

# Of Sulphuric Dying, and how the dead body may be made alive again, and placed into its first glory.

->Summary Points<-

1. Twofold desire in all life, §. 1. 2. namely the nature-desire, in which death arises, and the love-desire, in which life is born. 3. Nothing could make fallen man alive but the free delight <note>original: *Lust*; in this context, it refers to the divine will or the joy of God's presence.</note>. 4. The right **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: In Boehme’s alchemy, this is the "soul" of matter, the active principle that mediates between the dark, grasping nature and the light of the spirit.</term> is a birth of all spirituality and corporality, 5. and from the inner and outer Sulphur, man is created, 6. who was a perfect image of the Godhead, but through the delight fell into the 4 elements; 7. where the inner Sulphur faded, 8. whereby man lost his body of power <note>original: *Kraft-Leib*; a spiritual or "resurrection" body made of divine energy rather than coarse matter.</note>, 9. hence also the outer body dies. 10. There was no counsel; the love-desire had to enter into the wrath-desire, and extinguish and overcome the wrath with love, 11. wherein man's salvation consists. 12. How regeneration now happens in man: so also in metals. 13. 14. These must be brought into the **First Matter** <note>original: *primam Materiam*; the original, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made.</note>, and indeed through the Sulphur. 15. The body must be made hungry through a foreign fire, where the struggle of man with GOD begins, 16. in which he penetrates into GOD, and from love receives a new body, 17. into which he breathes the soul.

1. All life and movement, with reason and senses, both in living and growing things, stands in the original state in the Sulphur, as in the nature-desire, and in the freedom's delight-desire.

2. In the nature-desire arises death and the closing-in, and in the freedom's desire arises the opening-up and life, for the freedom's desire tinctures <note>original: *tingiret*; to permeate and transform the quality of a substance, like a dye or an alchemical catalyst.</note> the dark nature's desire, so that the fierce nature lets its own right sink, and gives itself to the freedom's desire; thus life grows in death. For without light there is no life; if the light in the essence of the Sulphur goes out, then it is an eternal death, for no one can make it alive, unless GOD moves in the delight-desire in the same death. For death can receive no life, unless the first desire—the desire of free delight—reveals itself in the desire for nature, wherein the closing-in as death is born.

4. 6. But man was good and completely perfect, created according to and out of all three worlds as an image of the Godhead in which God dwells; and he was the very essence itself that God is, according to eternity and according to time in all three worlds—yet a creature with a beginning, according to the nature of a creature. And he died to the heavenly and divine essence through delight <note>original: *Lust*; referring to the redirection of the human will or desire away from God toward selfhood.</note>. For the inner delight, which was born in the center as in the fire (in which the life stood in the divine essence—that is, it ignited the essence of divine gentleness, in which the joyful realm or angelic form stands), turned itself away from the inner delight of freedom and eternity and into time, into the "out-birth," into the planetary property, out of the pure divine element and into the four elements. Thus, the inner divine essence or inner corporality no longer possessed a leader or life.

### Summaries.

This [delight] gives itself freely into that [desire]. 4. Love reveals itself through fire, 12. and makes light out of darkness, and the light is the master of darkness. 13. All life, growth, and activity consists in two things: in Delight <note>original: "Lust"; in this context, it refers to a joyous, free expansion or "pleasure" rather than carnal desire.</note>, and in Desire <note>original: "Begierde"; a hungry, pulling force of longing or craving.</note>; Delight is a free will, and relative to nature it is to be regarded as a "Nothing," but Desire is like a hunger: In Desire, the driving spirit arises as the natural one, and in Delight arises the supernatural, which nevertheless belongs to nature, yet not out of its own self-property, but out of the property of Desire.

2. Desire is the driving of the essence as a hunger, and Delight is the essence of that hunger which it grasps within itself; for Desire is only a hungry will, and is the natural spirit in its forms; but Delight is from freedom, for GOD is without desire as far as His own being—insofar as He is called GOD—is concerned; for He needs nothing, everything is His, and He Himself is everything. But He has a Delight-Will, and He Himself is that same will, to reveal Himself in Delight; yet no revelation can occur in the free, affection-less Delight, for it is without desire; it is as if it were "nothing" compared to nature, and yet it is everything. But it is not everything according to Desire, as in nature, but according to the fulfillment of nature; it is the fulfillment of the hungry Desire, which is nature; it gives itself freely into the hunger of nature, for it is a spirit without essence and desire, entirely free as a "Nothing"; but Desire makes it into an essence within itself, and this according to two properties: one according to eternal freedom, which is free from torment, and the other according to Desire, which gives a vegetative life, as a growing or a giving of itself forth.

### XIV. On the Birth. Chapter 6.
<meta>catchword: desire,</meta>

[The] property gives a life to the oil: the oil is a light, and the property of **Desire** gives the light an essence, much like the fiery property, so that the light becomes a radiance, as one sees in fire and light. And yet, the free delight remains within itself a free will, but yields its **gentleness** as a free <term>yieldedness: or 'Gelassenheit'; the meditative state of letting go of the self-will to allow God to work within.</term> into the desire, so that it may come to substance and radiance. Its will is alone good; it has no other desire than only to be good, gentle, and lovely. There is also no other possibility within it, for it is as a "Nothing," in which no stirring or torment may exist, but is gentleness itself.

4. Since it then cannot be a "Nothing" because it is a cause and beginning of desire, it gives itself freely—just as the sunshine gives itself freely—into every property. Thus, the desire grasps this same free delight as the radiance of the <term>Ungrund: the 'groundless' or 'abyss'; the infinite mystery and nothingness out of which God and the universe emerge.</term> of eternity into itself, and makes it within itself according to its property in the essence: as much of the property as is in the desire, so much is also in the essence.

5. Thus, when the free delight yields itself into the hunger of the desire, the desire makes from the property of free delight a likeness according to that freedom—that is, as if it were nothing, and yet it is [something]; that is, a **water** and **oil**. But because the desire—that is, the hunger—is filled with the free delight, it also makes its own self-property in the essence of freedom into a substance: its essence is water, and the essence of the free delight is an oil. Thus, two kinds of properties arise in a single spirit: a fiery one according to the property of desire, and a joyful or **light-property** according to freedom.

6. The fiery one gives in its essence, as in its water, a sharpness from the strict desire; this is salted, or a **Salt**. And from the fiery anguish comes a **Sulphur**, out of which stones, earths, and metals have become in the <term>Impression: the process by which spiritual forces condense or 'press' themselves into material form.</term> and creation of the world, as well as elements and stars, all according to the forms in the desire. And the <term>oily: original: 'Olitätische'; the spiritual-chemical principle of oil, representing the cooling, soothing light.</term> gives its gentleness, as a love-delight, into it. The fiery property "impresses" with the desire and creates **corporeality**, and the oily property gives itself out in its gentleness and creates the **vegetable life** as a greening and growing within the fiery impression. 7. The Sages have called this form **Mercury**, from the anxious driving wheel <note>original: "ängstlichen treibenden Rade." In Böhme's thought, the "wheel of nature" represents the restless, circular motion of life and desire before it finds rest in God.</note>, which is the cause of all life and movement, and a master-worker in the <term>oily: or 'oleaginous'; referring to the spiritual principle of the 'Oil,' which Böhme sees as the medium through which the light of God flows.</term> and watery property.

For God has made all things out of Nothing, and that same Nothing is He Himself, as an indwelling Love-Delight wherein there is no <term>passion: or 'affect'; a state of being moved or disturbed by external things.</term>; but this Love-Delight would not be manifest if He remained alone in the stillness without essence, and there would be no joy or weaving activity <note>original: "Weben." This spirit stands against the wrath of the desire in Sulfur, Salt, and the poisonous **Mercury**, and stills and heals its poisonous hunger with the gentleness of Love; whatever Mercury breaks with the raging wheel of its own self-property, the delight of Love in the oil heals again; and thus there is evil and good in every life.

10. And yet there is no evil in any thing, unless the good or the Love-Oil languishes in its own delight; this happens in the forms of the <term>impression: the act of 'pressing in' or contracting, which Böhme associates with the hardening of spirit into matter.</term> of the hunger of desire. For example: if the hunger-spirit impresses itself too much into its own forms toward itself, and hungers too much after its own self-revelation, it cannot capture the free delight within itself which softens its hunger. For the property of nature should be <term>simply: or 'purely'; from the archaic 'schlecht,' meaning straight or direct.</term> directed toward the property of free delight—that is, toward God's Love-Essence—and direct its hunger toward Love; then the hunger receives Love into itself and makes it into an essence within itself. Then the hunger is no longer a languishing, dark hunger that stings and rages within itself like a poisonous Mercury, but becomes a love-desire out of the hunger, which is called **God’s Nature**; and the hungry, fiery nature is called **God’s Wrath**, and in the outer nature it is called a **fire**.

13. So that when the fire-glow of the light tastes sweetness, the fire-desire reaches for that meekness; thus the meekness of the free delight is entirely incomprehensible, like a Nothing. Now the hunger of the desire grasps its own self-essence and swallows it into itself, making it into Nothing. That is the darkness, which is the essence of the hunger; this the fiery hunger swallows through the property of the light or the free delight. As one sees: as soon as the light shines, it takes away the power of the darkness. Therefore, God is a Lord over all essence, for He is the eternal power and light, as we see by the metaphor of the Sun: it is a lord over the darkness and all essence, and governs everything that grows, lives, and weaves in this world.

The other Salt is the sharpness of the Impression according to the property of harsh strictness; that is the anxiety in the Impression, as **Sulfur**, and the essential property is **Water**. ### The 7th Chapter.

## How Adam was in Paradise, and Lucifer was a beautiful Angel, and how they were Corrupted through Imagination and Self-Elevation.

### Summaries.

1. The first Adam had heavenly eyes and was angelic; his life burned in a pure **Oil**, but in the Fall it became watery, § 1. 2.
2. when the cold **Saturn** <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, Saturn represents the contracting, chilling, and hardening force of nature</note> became elevated.
3. The Fall of **Lucifer** and **Adam** was that they wished to know and taste evil—the one seeking the fiery, the other the watery **Mercury**.
4–7. The serpent was from the Beginning.
8. God does not perish; rather, only the created **Mercury** is corrupted.
9. That which hungers after God is revealed in God;
10. but the devil created darkness for himself.
11. The birth of the serpent.
12. In the impression of the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; the creative command "Let there be," which Böhme describes as an "impression" or compaction of spiritual will into material form</note>, God and the world were separated.
13. In the highest **Mercury** lies the sharpest trial <note>original: "Prob"; a test or proof of quality</note>.
14. The proceeding out from the fire creates gentleness and gives two properties.

...the strongest **Mercury** <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurio*; the active, vibrating spirit that drives all movement and life</note>, lies hidden; that is an **Oil** <note>original: *Oel*; for Böhme, a symbol of the gentle, light-filled essence of life</note> that tinctures and drives away all sickness. ### Chapter 7. and the Signature of all Beings. 63

...set into the **Divine Kingdom of Joy** <note>original: *Göttliche Freudenreich*; Böhme’s term for the spiritual realm of light and bliss</note>, then the dead soul, which lay swallowed up in God’s curse, rises again. When the poisonous **Mercury** <term>Mercury</term> <note>the active, vibrating spirit that drives all movement; here, the restless human will</note>, which resembles God’s wrath, is <term>tinctured</term> <note>original: *tingiret*; an alchemical term for transforming a substance's inner essence through a spiritual agent</note> with Love, then out of the **death-anguish** in Mercury comes the highest Kingdom of Joy. This creates a desire for Love, which in turn produces a "Love-Being" within itself—a heavenly body emerging from the earthly one. When Mercury is placed into this heavenly quality, it no longer craves the earthly, deadly life or the **four elements**, but only the **One**, in which the four lie hidden, as if swallowed up. Just as light holds darkness swallowed within itself—the darkness exists, but it is not manifest in the light—so God dwells in Time, yet Time does not grasp Him, unless Time is caught up into Eternity so that the Divine Light shines within its agitation once more. Then, Time and all its wonders become manifest in Eternity.

26. Such is also the **Process of the Sages** <note>the path of the alchemists seeking the Philosopher's Stone</note> with the **Noble Stone**: one cannot contemplate this more deeply than to see how the **Eternal Word**—the heavenly, Divine Mercury—became human within Divine Power. It killed Death and placed the wrath within man (that is, the human Mercury) into the Divine Kingdom of Joy. There, the human Mercury, which previously lay locked in God’s wrath and death-torment, now draws **Divine Essence** (the Body of Christ) into itself through its newly-ignited desire, which is now called **Faith in the Holy Spirit**. It sets itself in Divine Power and Light above God's wrath and the serpent's poison, and it "treads upon the head" of wrath—the poison of death—with the life of the Divine Kingdom of Joy. That is to say: the wrath was the master, but in the Light it became a servant, which must now be a cause for joy. This is shown to us quite brightly and clearly, revealed entirely within the <term>mercurial</term> <note>original: *mercurialisch*; relating to the vital, transformative spirit of life</note> life, if we choose to contemplate it.

27. So, observe this process and meditate upon it, you dear children of the Sages, and you shall have enough for both time and eternity. Do not act as **Babel** <note>Böhme’s name for the corrupted institutional church and empty intellectualism</note> does, which tickles and comforts itself with the **Philosopher's Stone** and boasts of it, yet keeps only a "rough wall-stone"—locked in poison and death—instead of the Noble Stone of the Sages. What does it matter if Babel "has" the Stone, if the Stone remains entirely locked away in Babel? It is just as if a lord gave me a piece of land; it would indeed be mine, but if I could not occupy it, I would remain a poor man despite it.

# XIV. Of the Birth Chap. 7.

...and yet I boasted of dominion, thus possessing the name but not the power; so it goes with **Babel** <note>Böhme’s term for the confused, divided, and institutionalized church of his day</note> regarding the **Noble Stone** <term>Noble Stone</term> <note>the Philosopher’s Stone, which in Böhme's theology represents the spiritual transformation of the soul into Christ-like perfection</note> of the new rebirth in Christ Jesus.

28. In the most gracious name **JESUS CHRIST** we have the entire process contained: what and how the rebirth from death into life is. This is clearly understood in the **language of nature** <term>language of nature</term> <note>original: *Natur-Sprache*; the belief that the inherent sounds and structures of words reveal the true spiritual essence of the things they name</note>, for the name **JESUS** is the property of the free delight of eternity, which acts upon the center of the birth-giver—as if into the Father’s property—and is formed within that center of the Father’s property (the Father’s fire) into a Word of eternal power. Understand it thus:

29. The Father, as the fire-forms of the Father, shapes that same Divine Voice within the delight of freedom into an essence within Himself. That is to say, the Father’s fire-property makes itself into a **Mercury** <term>Mercury</term> <note>here meaning the active, moving spirit or "vibration" of divine life</note> of the Kingdom of Joy within the Divine Being of eternal love. For the Father's property is the **fire-source** <note>original: *Feuers-Quall*; Böhme uses this to describe the "welling up" or "agitation" of fire</note>, and the Son’s property—as the eternal delight—is the **love-source**. Yet there would be no desire for love if the Father’s fire did not ignite it and make it move with longing: for desire arises from the fire.

30. The Father of all beings gives birth to this holy desire through His fire-source; this is now His **Heart of Love**, which gives off its radiance and luster within His fire. There, from eternity to eternity, the **wrath** <note>original: *Grimm*; the harsh, consuming quality of God's judgment</note> dies away within the fire-property and is transmutated into a love-desire.

31. Note this: the property of free delight is called **Christ** here within the fire-property. In the language of nature, this means a "Breaker-through"—taking the power away from the wrath; a radiance of light in the darkness; a transmutation where the love-delight rules over the fire-delight (which is the wrath): light over darkness.

32. Here, the **Woman’s Seed** (understand this as the free delight, in which there is no torment or source-pain) treads upon the head of the wrath of eternal nature—the eternal desire. For the fire-property is rightly called the "head," as it is the cause of eternal life; and freedom (the free delight or the "Nothing") is rightly called the "Woman," for the birth of the **Holy Trinity** of the Godhead stands within that "Nothing," which is the freedom from all source-pain.

# Chapter 7 and the Designation of all Beings.

...Being into life, and within Being is the birth, as the Father, as the eternal ground, brings forth His Being as His Heart out of the **Groundless** <term>Groundless</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*; Böhme’s term for the absolute void or "nothingness" that precedes God’s self-manifestation</note> within Himself—that is, out of the Groundless into a Ground. The Son becomes the Father’s ground. Thus the Father remains in Himself, regarding only His own property, the ground of eternal nature; and the Son remains in the Father as the ground of power and the Kingdom of Joy, just as you see an analogy in fire and light. And so the Son **tinctures** <term>tinctures</term> <note>from the alchemical *tinctura*; to permeate, color, or fundamentally transform the nature of a substance</note> the Father with freedom, as if with "Nothingness," and the Father tinctures the Nothingness so that it becomes an eternal life within Him, and no longer a Nothingness, but rather a resonance or voice of the revelation of eternity.

34. Therefore, you dear wise ones, take note here of what the ground is, if you wish to tincture. Do not seek the Son outside of the Father if you wish to tincture; there must be a **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*; implying that the spiritual transformation must take place within a physical or substantial reality</note>. The **Serpent-Crusher** <note>a reference to Christ as the one who fulfills the prophecy of Genesis 3:15</note> already lies within it; for it was not outside of humanity that the seed of the woman crushed the serpent’s head, but rather within humanity. The **welling source** <note>original: *Quall*; Böhme uses this word to imply both a "source" (*Quelle*) and the "agitation/torment" (*Qual*) of life forces</note> of Divine Delight (understand this as Love) revealed itself through an awakening in the human essence, and became manifest in human life. It tinctured the **wrath** <note>original: *Grimm*; the harsh, consuming fire of God's justice or "dark" nature</note> of death with the blood of the Divine Tincture. There, out of the wrath of death, a welling source of Divine Love and a Kingdom of Joy was formed. Thus, Love crushed the head of the anger and the oily poison within **Mercury** <term>Mercury</term> <note>in Böhme's alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of movement, sound, and sensation, which can be either poisonous/wrathful or life-giving</note>. It took the power away from the wrath and placed that wrath into the highest Kingdom of Joy; there, anger and bitter, cold death were put on display within a fiery love. Then it was said:

> Death, where is your sting? Hell, where is your victory? <note>original: *Tod wo ist dein Stachel; Hölle wo ist dein Sieg?*</note>

Praise be to God, who has given us the victory. 1 Cor. 15:55.

35. So it now belongs to the wise man who wishes to seek, that he consider the entire process of the humanity of Christ—from His opening in the body of His mother Mary, until His resurrection and ascension. Then he will surely find the **Feast of Pentecost** with the joy-filled Spirit, with which he may tincture, cure, and heal that which is broken. We say this with the foundation of truth, as we have highly recognized it.

36. The **Time of the Lily** <note>a prophetic era of spiritual purity and peace often mentioned by Böhme</note> leading to a Rose, which will bloom in May when the winter passes; to the godless it shall be a blindness, and to the seeing, a light.

For the body you are to heal is half-dead and severely wounded; moreover, its proper clothing has been stripped off, so that you would hardly recognize the man you are to heal unless you had the Samaritan's eyes and will, seeking nothing through them except to restore the damage of the wounded man.

But when the soul-fire in Adam poisoned the will-spirit in Adam through the Devil’s infection and introduced it into earthly, deadly lust through the serpent’s property, the heavenly Mercury withdrew from the heavenly essence. That is, the soul’s will departed from it with its desire and led its hunger into the earthly, deadly being—into the property of the cold Mercury that had made stones and earth. Adam’s spirit wanted to test this and have the knowledge of good and evil.

# Chapter 7 and the Designation of All Beings.

42. ...into his poison, and worked within him, and robbed him of his divine property; it stung and wounded him with heat and cold, and made him half-dead, and stripped off his angelic garment—that garment which existed in the pure element, where the heavenly **agitation** <note>original: *Qual*; Böhme uses this term to mean both a "source-quality" and the "anguish" or "striving" of life's forces</note> permeated through the four elements and **tinctured** <term>tinctured</term> <note>To "tincture" means to permeate something with a new quality or essence, much like a dye changes a fabric or a medicine heals a body</note> them in Adam’s body. Back then, he needed no other clothing, for heat and cold were within him as if swallowed up, just as the day keeps the night swallowed up within it; and though the night dwells in the day, it is not manifest. So it went with man: when the property and anguish of the night seized him, it began to rule within him. And so it also went with the earth when God cursed it.

43. If you now wish to be a **Magus** <term>Magus</term> <note>A spiritual seeker who understands the hidden signatures of God in nature and how to work with the spiritual "mercury" of the soul</note>, then you must have the understanding of how you can **transmute** <term>transmutiren</term> the night back into day. For the night, as the anguish of darkness, is the deathly anguish of the soul; and the day, as the agitation of the light, is life and a shine within life. Christ rekindled this shine within humanity once more and made it alive again within man. If you now wish to **tincture** <term>tingiren</term>, you must transmute that which is "locked away"—that which lies locked in the death of night—back into the day; for the day is the **Tincture**, and yet day and night lie within one another as one single being.

44. Now **Reason** <note>represented here as the skeptical or limited human intellect that struggles to understand spiritual mysteries</note> speaks: "How should I look upon this, so that I may do it?" Look then at the process, how God began it with humanity when He wished to tincture it.

45. Christ came into this world in the locked-up human form and brought the **Tincture** of life—which is the Godhead—into the enclosure of death. He came into the world as a guest, in our poor form; He became one of us so that He might tincture us within Himself. But what did He do? Did He live in joys? Did He carry Himself as a Lord? No, He went into death and died, and He cast off the anguish of the night within Himself on our behalf. But how did He do it? He took our soul’s and body’s **essence** <term>Essenz</term> into the **Divine Essence**, and He joined our essence with the Divine, so that our essence entered back into the Divine Essence with its will and desire. Thus the heavenly **Fiat** <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin for "Let it be done"; referring to the creative command of God that brings life from nothing</note> became active again in humanity, for humanity then integrated itself back into **freedom**, into the free delight of the Godhead.

### XIV. Of the Birth Chapter 7.

52. You say: Name the Baptism for me; and I have already named it for you. Every hunger is a desire according to its own property: But if you give the hunger of death the property of death again, then death grows; however, if you give it the heavenly property, death does not accept it, for hell is against heaven. Thus, you must give death to death and to the **Wrath of GOD**: and in that same wrath, give it the Heavenly Being, as the Baptism; then the Baptism will swallow up death within itself. In that case, the wrath dies in death through the Baptism, but not immediately; you must first hold to the *Process of Christ* <note>The "Process of Christ" refers to the developmental stages of a believer's life mirroring Christ's life, death, and resurrection.</note>, and must let the baptized one preach—that is, let him shine forth with his own Divine form and colors—pursue and plague him vehemently, and leave him no rest, for it is in this way that the true <term>Mercurius|Mercury, understood here as the vital, animating spirit or "workman" within matter and soul</term> becomes active.

53. There Christ will arise from death and show himself, but only His own people recognize Him; He thus walks about in a hidden form, and sometimes in His own, until the Feast of Pentecost. Acts 2:41.

54. But your greedy death holds you back and keeps you locked away. Because you seek greed and worldly honor in worldly pleasure, thereby bearing yourselves in the property of the Night, the <term>Perlein</term> hides itself from you. However, the day will shine again when the fierce **Wrath of GOD** shall be fulfilled in the blood of the saints, softened, and become a Love-life: And the time is near.

### The Actual Process of Forming the Magical Child.

60. It shows how the child arises from the essence of the parents, but upon the ignition of its own true life, it casts away the parents' vegetable nature and activity. Like its own plant—as a new, independent effect—it arises according to the properties of the newly ignited spirit. In this way, the child becomes nobler than its parents, specifically regarding their external life.

61. Rather, we mean the magical soul: how eternity, as the Godhead in His likeness, according to the model of Wisdom, imagines itself into all things, and how God fulfills all. In this way, we understand the <term>Highest Good|original: "Summum Bonum"</term>, the good treasure that lies locked away within the essence of the external world, as if in <term>Paradise|original: "Paradeiß"</term>.

72. 73. <note>original: "Summa"</note> In summary, the whole Work, about which people speak so wondrously much, consists of two things: a heavenly and an earthly. The heavenly is meant to take the earthly into itself to make it heavenly; eternity is to take time into itself to make it eternity. The Artist seeks Paradise; if he finds it, he possesses the greatest treasure on Earth. However, one dead person does not wake another; the Artist must be alive if he wishes to say to the mountain: "Rise up and cast yourself into the sea" <note>original: "Matth. 21: 21"</note> (Matthew 21:21).

74. When the embodiment of the child begins, <term>Saturn|Saturnus; the first property of nature, characterized by contraction, cold, and darkness</term> first seizes it. Then it is dark and of little value, and it is mocked because such a mystery lies hidden in such a foolish form. Here, Christ walks upon the earth in a simple, poor, and weary form, like a guest; and He does not even have as much space or property in Saturn as a place to lay His head. He walks as a stranger, as if He were not at home there.

75. Afterwards, the <term>Moon|Mond; the property of formation and physical manifestation</term> seizes it; there, the heavenly and earthly properties are mingled, and the <term>vegetable life|vegetabilische Leben; the basic life force of growth found in plants</term> arises. The Artist rejoices at this, yet the process is still in danger here.

76. After the Moon, <term>Jupiter|Jupiter; the property of light, reason, and gentle power</term> seizes it. # XIV. On the Birth Chapter 7.

Or if the <term>Artist|Künstler; the alchemist or spiritual seeker</term> wishes to be so diligent as to warm the bed for the two <term>spouses|Eh-leute; the active and passive principles, often Sulfur and Mercury</term>, he must take great care not to anger them in their love. Whatever he begins, he must see through to the end. However, the <term>Groom|Bräutigam; the masculine/earthly principle</term> is unpredictable; he always possesses a dual will: an earthly hunger for God’s wrath, and a hunger for his <term>Bride|Braut; the feminine/heavenly principle</term>. 73. In summary, the whole Work—about which people speak so much and so strangely—consists of two things: a heavenly and an earthly. The Artist seeks <term>Paradise|Paradeis</term>; if he finds it, he possesses the greatest treasure on earth. But a dead man does not wake another dead man. 79. He must deal with his undertaking as the world dealt with Christ; only then can he find Paradise, wherein no death dwells.

80. But if he is not himself in that same birth of restoration, and does not walk the path that Christ walked on Earth—entering into Christ’s spirit and will—then let him abandon the search. ### Chap. 8. and the Description of All Beings.

...in joy and gentleness, and the deadly in the anguish of darkness; and yet one is the cause of the other. Light is the death, dying, and destruction of darkness (as anguish): for in the light, anguish has no power, but is instead <term>transmuted|original: transmutiret—to change from one substance or state into another</term> into the exaltation of the kingdom of joy, and becomes the cause of joy; otherwise there would be no joy, for gentleness on its own is still; but the torment of anguish makes it exultant, like a laugh. Thus anguish, as darkness, is the death and destruction of the <term>oily|original: Olitätischen—referring to the light-bearing, spiritual essence of oil</term> property; for if it gains the upper hand in the oily property, it takes over the <term>body|original: Corpus</term> and turns the oil into a poisonous torment, as a dark spirit and body—becoming entirely earthly, as Adam became when he <term>imagined|original: imaginirte—to focus one's creative desire or will toward an object</term> into evil.

9. And yet we should not understand it as the <term>oily|original: Olitätische</term> property taking on a poisonous quality itself; rather, <term>mercury|original: Mercurius—the active, mobile spirit or "fire-life"</term>, as the fire-life, leads itself into anguish and poisons the being of time—which the outer mercury does himself in his own desire; that is, he goes out from the inner oily being, so the inner remains standing immovable in itself, and the being and spirit of time separates from the being and spirit of eternity. And yet there is no total severing, but two <term>principles|original: Principia</term> remain in One being, where there are indeed two beings, but one does not grasp the other, just as time does not grasp eternity. For thus also Adam and Eve died: the soulful mercury went out from the being of eternity with his <term>imagination|original: Imagination</term> into the being of time, into the torment of anguish; there the being of eternity lost its guide, and Christ brought him back again with the Divine Word or mercury. Thus the being of eternity—which was in Adam and had been abandoned by the soulful mercury—received life again. And so we know that in the anxious mercury, the being of eternity lies hidden, as if in the closure of death.

10. And this is our writing and teaching: how one might bring the poisonous mercury with its desire so far that it enters again with its desire into the being of eternity, as into that which is locked away, and takes on the being of eternity again as a body, and with the same <term>tinctures|original: tingire—to permeate, color, or transform a substance through alchemical "tincture"</term> the being of time and brings them into one, so that the entire <term>body|original: Corpus</term> of the inner and outer world is only one, so that there is only one will in the spirit, as a love-hunger; thus that same hunger also makes for him...
