11. Thus we understand that joy and sorrow, love and enmity, all originate through **Imagination** <note>original: "Imagination" — in this context, it refers to the creative power of the mind or will to "image" or pull something into being</note> and desire; for in the desire toward **GOD**, as toward free love, the kingdom of joy arises in the midst of the **anguish of death**. And if the longing goes out from free love and into the **anguish of death**, as into the torment of darkness, then the longing is filled with the death-torment; thus also **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius" — the active, mobile spirit or "fire-life" in alchemy</note> operates in death-torment.

12. Therefore we say with good reason: That no thing is so evil that a good does not lie within it, though the wickedness is not capable of receiving it. Likewise, within the poisonous **Mercury** lies the greatest Pearl-Jewel: if his poisonous will can be led into that [goodness], then he himself reveals the pearl, for he <term>transmutes|original: transmutiret—to change from a base state to a higher or more refined state</term> himself. This can be seen in the earth, where **Mercury** seeks his pearl and, in the coarse stone, turns it into gold and other metals, all according to how the **Sulphur** <note>original: "Sulphur" — the substantial or "oily" principle that provides the fuel for the spirit's fire</note> is in each place.

13. For there is a constant wrestling in the earth; Eternity longs to be set free from the time of vanity. In its longing, it yields itself to **Mercury** as its life and master-workman. When **Mercury** receives this into his hunger, he becomes full of joy and makes that same free desire bodily within himself—that is gold and silver, along with other metals and good herbs, all according to the power of each place. As the "boiling" or "seething" <note>original: "Sud" — a term for the internal geological/alchemical heat brewing substances in the earth</note> is in each place, so also is the metal, all according to the property of the <term>seven forms of nature|original: sieben Gestälte der Natur—the seven core qualities Böhme believed governed all existence</term>. Whichever form is the <term>primary|original: Primas</term> in a place, according to that property a metal grows, as do herbs and trees.

14. In this, the **Physician** <note>original: "Medico"</note> must take note and learn to recognize the distinction—which property is the strongest in each thing with which he wishes to cure. If he does not know this, he will often give his patient death. He must also know the property of the patient, and which of the seven forms of nature characterizes the **Mercury** within the **Sulphur**; for it is such a **Salt** <note>original: "Saltz" — the physical, stabilizing principle in alchemy</note> that he produces. If the **Physician** gives him a contrary Salt, **Mercury** will only be further enraged by it and become more poisonous. But if he can receive his own **Salt** according to his property (for which he hungers), then he rejoices and lets his poisonous torment sink into **Mars's fire** <note>original: "Martis Feuer" — the hot, aggressive, or wrathful quality of nature</note>.

15. The other [way] is dangerous and uncertain; if he happens to succeed, it is a matter of luck and an unstable condition, and he cannot drive any disease out from its foundation. For the external **Mercury** is locked away; it cannot reach further than into the four **elements** <note>original: "Elementa"</note>, into the deadly essence; it has no power in the sidereal [starry] body. But if it is turned around and led into love, as mentioned above, then it attacks the root and the foundation, and renovates right up to the Divine Power, to the other **Principle** <note>original: "Principium" — in Böhme’s system, the second Principle is the world of light and divine love</note>.

16. It leads this into its hungry, fiery **Mars-desire** <note>original: "Martis-Begierde" — referring to the planet Mars as the source of aggressive, driving energy or "sting"</note>, into its **Salt**, as into its bodily essence, into **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur" — the substantial or "oily" principle that provides the fuel for the spirit's fire</note>, which is its mother; and it leads it around with its rotation in the **essence**, as if it were cooking with it. Then freedom, as the highest power, reaches for its own property—the **solar** property—and seizes the **Mercury** along with it.

17. Now, when **Mercury** tastes the heavenly within itself, it becomes desirous of the power of love and draws it into its desire. By this, it <term>transmutes|original: transmutiret—to change from a base state to a higher or more refined state</term> itself and its **Salt**, as well as its mother **Sulfur**, into a lovely source-quality <note>original: "Qual" — here meaning a "working quality" or "living source" rather than the modern German meaning of "torment"</note>. And when freedom is thus led into a moving life with **Mercury**, it is full of joy and rises in its joy like a gleam from the fire, breaking through the **Sulfur-spirit** in the **Salt**. This is the growth of the root; and from this, the root receives such a lovely scent and taste. For in the primordial state, the sharpness of the **Salt** in the first <term>impression|original: Impression—the compressive force of the spirit contracting into matter</term> from **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturno" — the planet representing cold, contraction, and death</note> is a sharpness of death-anguish; but here it becomes a lovely power, for all taste in herbs is **Salt**.

18. Thus, understand further regarding the root in the earth: when the inner power of freedom presses forth from itself toward the revelation of the Godhead within the property of **Mercury** (which is now transmuted), the sun's power presses toward the Divine Power and appropriates it with great desire

Deep within there lies the property of the inner and outer sun, as the inner and outer power, each property in its own **principle** <note>original: "Principio" — In Böhme's cosmology, a Principle is one of three fundamental realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light world of God, and the physical world of the four elements.</note>. If you wish to be called **Doctor** and Master, then you should also know how you may **transmute** the external **Mercury** within the **sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur" — the alchemical principle of substance and combustion; here, it represents the soul's inner fire which must be turned from "anguish" into "love."</note> into love, so that it is released from the torment of anguish and placed into a kingdom of joy—the earthly into a heavenly, death into a life. That is your **doctorate** <note>Böhme argues that a true doctor of medicine or theology must understand spiritual transformation through divine grace, rather than just physical or intellectual learning.</note> in the right sense, and not through the **steward** <term>steward|original: Amtmann — usually refers to the "spirit of this world" or the limited laws of nature and human reason</term> of reason alone.

28. God has set man over the **steward** and ordered him into understanding as into his own **dominion** <note>original: "Regiment".</note>. He has the power to **transmute** nature and to change the evil into a good; but he can do this only if he has first **transmuted** himself; otherwise, he cannot. As long as he is dead in his understanding, so long is he the **steward's** servant and minister; but when he becomes alive in God, then the **steward** becomes his servant.

29. You proud little hats <note>A mocking reference to the academic caps worn by university doctors and scholars.</note>, let me tell you: pride and self-honor, as well as earthly fleshly lust, lie in your way, so that you are not masters of the mysteries, but rather [blind]...

Then freedom presses out of itself into the property of Mercury, and Mercury always separates Saturn and Mars from it, for he wishes to have a beautiful child for his joy. He lets **Venus** <term>Venus|original: Venus — the property of love, sweetness, and external beauty</term> remain with the child, for she is related to the child in her property. Copper is closest to gold because of its matter; it only lacks the tincture, as Mars holds it too harshly in his possession. If Mars can be removed from it, it becomes gold, which the artist well understands.

33. For in the gentleness of Venus, the Sun glimmers forth; he cooks his food with his own fire and requires no artist for it—which the artist should well note—for he has his Mars within himself.

37. Now, in that same oil is the hunger, or the Love-Desire, for the being of time, as if for the revelation of the Deity. It gives itself out in its joy into the harsh quality of the fruit, and softens them all with the love which it receives in the Center, in the oil of freedom. Thus, a fruit which was initially sour and harsh becomes entirely lovely and sweet, so that a person may eat it. And such is the ripening of all fruits.

Unless it be that he burns that same herb into ash and gives it to him, then the poison of the loathing consumes the power, for that same ash is a death to the poison of the living Mercury. 44. If the doctor knew the nature of this loathing and prepared a **Jovial** cure according to the hunger of the patient's own spirit or Mercury, that would be correct. However, if the Moon’s property were strong in the salt he intended to give against the loathing, he would only be giving the patient more loathing. But if the Jovial cure were free from the Moon, then the Jovial Mercury would take its own food with great desire and leave the loathing. It is the same with diseases that arise in the **Salniter** <term>Salniter|The "saltpeter of the earth"—not just a chemical, but the explosive, vital, and creative force within nature and the human body</term> as if from a **fright** <note>original: "Erſchrecken" or "Schrack"</note>; there, only such a shock is required as the first one was, and the cure is already there; or such a herb where the Salniter lies in the same property as it does in that person.

Was it in the world or outside the world? Did Paradise stand in God's power or in the elements? Was the power of God manifest in the world or hidden? For it is written: *Do I not fill all things?* (Jeremiah 23:24). Likewise: *Thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, from eternity.* (Matthew 6:13).

# XIV. On the Birth. Chapter 8.

46. For He Himself is everything, but He is not called "God" according to every essence, but rather according to the Light <note>original: "Lichte" — in this context, the "Light" is the aspect of God that is love, clarity, and holiness, as opposed to the "Darkness" of His wrath or raw power</note>. With that Light, He dwells within Himself and shines with power through all His essences; He imparts His power to all His essences and works, and every thing receives His power according to its own quality; one receives Darkness, the other Light; every hunger desires its own quality, and yet the whole of essence is entirely God’s, whether it be evil or good: For from Him and through Him is everything; whatever is not of His love, is of His wrath.

47. Paradise is still in the world, but man is not in it, unless he be reborn from God; if so, according to that same new rebirth, he is within it, and not with the four-elemental <term>Adam|The "four-elemental Adam" refers to the physical, mortal human body composed of the four elements (earth, air, fire, water), which replaced the spiritual, paradisiacal body after the Fall.</term>: If only we would learn to know ourselves, we would understand it through the created essence.

48. 49. So also, in the same way, God dwells in all things, and the thing knows nothing of God; He is also not manifest to the thing, and yet it receives power from Him; but according to its quality, either from His love or from His wrath <note>original: "Grimme" — often translated as "fury" or "fierceness," this refers to the harsh, consuming fire of God's nature when not tempered by Light.</note>; and from whichever it takes, so it marks itself in the outward appearance. And yet the good is also within it, but entirely enclosed, just like wickedness; as you have an example of this in a thorn bush, and in other prickly things, out of which a beautiful, sweet-smelling flower grows. Two qualities lie within it, one lovely and one hostile; whichever triumphs forms the fruit.

50. So too was man created as a beautiful Paradise-flower and fruit: But the Devil awakened his thorny quality through the serpent—understand the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum" — the inner core or spiritual origin point from which all properties emerge.</note>

# Chapter 9. And the Description of all Beings.

...and the seventh day is perfection, wherein the six rest; It is the center, where the six run with their desire: Therefore God called it the Sabbath or Day of Rest; for within it, the six <term>properties|original: Gestalten — also translated as "forms" or "qualities"</term> of the working power rest. It is the Divine Sound within the power, or the <term>realm of joy|original: Freudenreich</term>, in which all the other properties become manifest; for it is the <term>composed Word|original: gefaste Wort — the Word of God brought into a structured or tangible form</term>, or the Divine Corporeality, through which all things were born into being and arrived.

3. This same composed Word has revealed itself through the movement of all properties within this visible world, as if through a visible <term>likeness|original: Gleichniß — a parable or symbolic reflection</term>, so that the spiritual essence might stand revealed in a physical, comprehensible form: Just as the desire of the inner form has made itself external, so the Inner stands within the Outer; the Inner holds the Outer before itself as a mirror, in which it beholds itself in the quality of the procreation of all forms. The Outer is its <term>Signature|original: Signatur — the external mark or shape that reveals an object's inner spiritual essence</term>.

4. Thus, every thing that has been born from the Inner has its signature. The highest form, which is the supreme one in the spirit of operation within the power, marks the *body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note> most clearly; to this one, the other forms are attached, as can be seen in all living creatures in the shape of the body, in their habits and gestures; in the sound, voices, and languages, as well as in trees, herbs, stones, and metals. Just as the struggle is within the power of the spirit, so stands the figure of the body; and thus is its will, as long as the <term>seething|original: Sud — an alchemical term for the boiling or brewing of spiritual and physical elements</term> in the spirit-life boils in that manner.

5. But if the <term>Artist|original: Künstler — here referring to an alchemist or one who understands the secrets of nature</term> approaches it with the right *Mercury* <note>original: "Mercurio" — in alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of transformation and the "master-craftsman" of form</note> in which the seething stands, he may turn the weakest form to the top and the strongest to the bottom. Then the spirit receives a different will, according to that supreme form which previously had to be a servant; that form then becomes master among the seven properties. Just as *Christ* <note>original: "Christus"</note> said to the sick: "Arise, your faith has helped you," and he stood up. So, in like manner, every form hungers for the center; and the center is the sound of life, namely *Mercury*; he is the master-builder or shaper of the power. If this same sound surrenders itself to the hunger of the lowest form in the struggling power, then it swings its quality (understand: the quality of that specific form) into the heights.

There is nothing in the essence of all essences that does not have the seven properties within itself; for they are the wheel of the *center*, the causes of the *sulfur* <note>original: Sulphuris — the combustible or "soul" principle in alchemy</note>, in which *Mercury* creates the *seething* <note>original: Sud</note> in the <term>anguish-source|original: Angst-Qual — the state of tension or "labor" within nature that precedes the manifestation of light</term>.

### Chapter 9. and the Signature <note>original: "Bezeichnung" — often referring to the 'signature' or outward mark of an inner spiritual essence</note> of all Beings.

When <term>Saturn|Representing lead, contraction, and the foundational physical structure</term> is nearest, the decoction <note>original: "Sud" — the alchemical 'boiling' or ripening process of matter</note> in the <term>Sulphur of Saturn|The soul-principle or essential oil associated with the planet Saturn</term> gives a long, strong body, for she gives her sweetness into <term>Saturn’s</term> Impression <note>the 'imprinting' of a planetary quality into matter</note>, from which <term>Saturn</term> becomes quite joyful; and if <term>Venus|Representing copper, love, and formative beauty</term> is not hindered by <term>Mars|Representing iron, heat, and raw energy</term>, it becomes a large, long, plain <note>original: "schlechter" — in this historical context meaning simple, straightforward, or honest, rather than 'bad'</note> tree, herb, animal, or human, whatever it may be.

32. The <term>Magus|A practitioner of natural and divine magic</term> may take note of [and use] this; it resists all malice and the false interference of spirits, whatever they may be, so long as a human does not himself become false and incline his desire toward the devil, as Adam did, in whom the <term>Universal</term> was also once complete.

The curse of God covers the sight of the evil eye so that it does not see it, even if it were standing before its eyes; however, in such a conjunction <note>An alignment of planets</note> of the planets, they are manifest and cannot hide themselves.

### Chapter 9. and the Designation of all Beings.

40. The herb also becomes rough and a little prickly; the little branches on the leaves, as well as the stem, are subtle according to <term>Venus’s</term> manner, but the power is that of <term>Mars</term> and <term>Jupiter</term>, mixed and well-tempered, usually with brownish flowers, penetrating in its property. This is because <term>Mars</term> is strong within it with his wrath; but because his wrath is transformed by <term>Jupiter</term> and <term>Venus</term> into a friendly property, the wrath becomes a desire for joy.

41. 42. Cold is entirely contrary to him.

43. He should first temper <term>Mars</term> and <term>Mercury</term> and set them into joy; then it is truly good.

44. The hotter a herb is, the better it is for this purpose, provided that the fire-wrath in it is transformed into love; thus it can also transform the wrath in the body into joy, all according to the property of the disease, so that the disease may endure it.

# XIV. On the Birth Chapter 9.

...how greatly the <note>mercurial</note> poison might ignite, or lead into another hostile torment: To be sure, he should use the **martial** <note>associated with Mars</note> and **mercurial** <note>associated with Mercury</note> salt for the **cure**; but he must first reconcile **Mars** and **Mercury** with **Venus** and **Jupiter**, so that both of those angry forces surrender their will into the will of **Jupiter**, so that **Jupiter**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** all three receive One Will in their power. 54. **Reason** <note>original: "Ratio"</note> also has its **cure** through its likeness: Just as a sickness can be introduced into the **senses** <note>original: "Sensibilia"</note> through words, so that the reason becomes sick and tormented, and finally leads to heavy sickness and death; so also can it be cured with the opposite of that same thing. ### Chapter 9. and the Signature of all Beings.

...and <note>tincture—an alchemical term meaning to transform or imbue with a new quality</note> the Mercury in the soul again with love, so his Sun in the soul will shine again, and his Jupiter will rejoice.

57. If you say now, "I cannot, I am too greatly imprisoned," then I say: I also cannot, for it does not lie in my willing, running, and racing, but it lies in **God's** mercy. For I cannot by my own power take away the power of the fierce wrath of **God** which is ignited within me. But because His dear heart, out of love and in love, has entered again into humanity—as if into the poisonous, ignited Mercury in the soul—and has tinctured the soul as the poison-source of eternal nature with the quality of the eternal Father's nature, I will therefore cast my will into His transformation. I will, with my will, depart from the ignited poison-source, out of the evil Mercury in **God’s** wrath, and enter into His death. I will die in and with Him through my corrupted will, and become a Nothing in Him. Then He must become my life. For if my will is Nothing, then He is in me whatever He wills; then I no longer know myself as belonging to me, but to Him.

58. If He wills that I should be something, let Him make it so; but if He wills not, then I am dead in Him; so let Him live in me as He wills. If I am then a Nothing, I am at last in the Essence from which my father Adam was created, for out of the Nothing **God** has made all things.

59. The Nothing is the highest good, for there is no <term>Turba</term> <note>original Latin: "turba"; Böhme uses this to describe a state of inward disruption, turmoil, or the "awakened wrath" that destroys the harmony of a being</note> within it. Thus, nothing can touch me, for I am nothing to myself; rather, I am **God's**, who knows what I am; I do not know it, nor should I know it. And thus is the cure for my soul's sickness; whoever will venture it with me will experience what **God** will make of him. As an example, I state:

60. I write here, and yet I do not do it; for I, who am the "I" that I am, know nothing and have not learned it. So I do not do it, but **God** does in me what He wills. I am aware of nothing in myself, but I know in Him what He wills. Thus, I do not live for myself, but for Him; and thus we are only One in Christ, like one tree with many boughs and branches, and He bears fruit in every little branch as He wills. And so I have brought His life into mine, so that I am reconciled with Him in His love.

## XIV. Concerning the Birth, Chapter 9.

61. For His will in Christ has entered into humanity—into me—so now my will within me enters into His humanity; and thus His living <term>Mercury<note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the "speaking Word" or the active, vibrating power of life. Here, the divine Mercury heals the disordered, "poisonous" Mercury of the fallen human soul.</note></term>—that is, His Word, as the speaking Mercury—tinctures my fierce, evil Mercury, and transmutes mine into His. And so my <term>Mars<note>Mars represents the fiery, energetic, and often wrathful aspect of the soul. Under divine influence, this "wrath-fire" is transformed into "love-fire."</note></term> has become a love-fire of **GOD**, and His Mercury speaks through mine, as through His instrument, whatever He wills; and thus my <term>Jupiter<note>Jupiter represents the principle of light, wisdom, and gentle joy within the soul's inner cosmos.</note></term> lives in the joys of **GOD**, and I do not even know it; the true Sun shines upon me, and I do not see it: For this is the reason:

62. I do not live for myself, and I do not see for myself, and I do not know for myself. I am a thing, and I know not what, for **God** knows what I am. So I run along as a thing, just as the Spirit drives me within the thing, and thus I live according to my inner will, which is nevertheless not my own.

63. But I find yet another life in me, which is what I am—not according to <term>surrender<note>original: "Gelassenheit." A key term in German mysticism referring to the state of "yieldedness" or "letting go" of the individual ego to God.</note></term>, but according to the creature of this world, as a likeness of eternity. That same life still stands in poison and strife, and is yet to become Nothing; only then will I be entirely perfect. So now, in that same life wherein I still feel my <term>selfhood<note>original: "Ichheit." The sense of "I-ness" or the ego that separates the individual from God.</note></term>, there is sin and death; these must come to nothing. For in the life that **God** is within me, I am an enemy to sin and death; but according to the life that is still in my selfhood, I am an enemy to the Nothing (which is the Godhead).

64. Thus one life strives against the other, and there is a constant struggle within me. But because Christ is born in me, and lives in my <term>nothingness<note>original: "Nichtheit." The state of having emptied the self of its own will.</note></term>, Christ shall indeed—according to His promise made in <term>Paradise<note>original: "Paradeis." Refers to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note></term>—crush the head of the serpent (which is my selfhood) and kill the evil man in my selfhood, so that He who is Himself may live.

65. But what shall Christ do with the evil man; shall He cast him away? No, for he is in heaven, and performs his wonders in this world, which stands in the curse. So now each works in his own sphere: the outer man works in the cursed world, which is both evil and good, within the wonders of **God**, as in the mirror of glory which is yet to be revealed in him; and the inner man is not his own, but the instrument of **GOD**, with which **God** does whatever He wills, until the outer man with his wonders in the mirror...

66. But when the inner penetrates the outer and leads its sunshine through it, and the outer receives the sunshine of the inner, it is <term>tinctured<note>original: "tingiret." In alchemy and Böhme’s theology, a "tincture" is a spiritual essence that can penetrate, transform, and "dye" a lower substance into a higher state.</note></term>, cured, and healed by the inner; and the inner shines through it, just as the sun shines through water, or as a fire glows through iron. Then it needs no other cure.

67. But because the Devil stands against the soul in the wrath of eternal nature as an enemy of souls, and always directs his poisonous imagination toward the soul to tempt it; and since the anger or <term>wrath<note>original: "Grimm." This refers to the harsh, fiery, and judgmental quality of nature that exists apart from God's light.</note></term> of eternal nature is manifest in the outer man—which Adam awakened—this same wrath is often awakened by the Devil and his servants, so that it operates and burns in the outer body. Then the inner love-fire is extinguished in the outer man, just as a glowing iron is extinguished in water—not immediately in the inner man, but in the outer. This happens if the outer man remains lying in the water of sins, and if the soul (which had previously surrendered itself into the "Nothing," as into freedom, into the life of **GOD**) enters with its desire into the outer sinful man; then it loses the inner sun, for it goes out of the "Nothing" back into the "Something," which is the state of torment.

68. 70. So it is also with man: From whichever light man lives, from that same light his cure also comes. If he lives for the outer world, then the outer goodness and love—such as the outer <term>Jupiter<note>Representing wisdom and benevolence.</note></term> and <term>Venus<note>Representing love and beauty.</note></term> with the Sun—must be his cure; otherwise, he remains imprisoned in the angry <term>Mars<note>The force of fire and conflict.</note></term> and in the poisonous Mercury, in the earthly Moon, in the <term>Impression of Saturn<note>original: "Impression Saturni." The combustible "body" or "substance" within nature.</note></term>, which was awakened and made manifest in the outer man with Adam. For this reason, the outer man must die, rot, and thus enter into nothingness—into the end, or better said, into the beginning of creation, into the essence from which he departed with Adam.

46. It did not make it into Saturn; rather, it holds it locked in the Saturnian death.

So, let the devil set fire to his mother's house with his fury and tempt him; he will now surely protect himself from the devil with Christ.

64. This shall come to pass: when the Tempter comes and attacks him, the youth with the virginal heart will surrender himself entirely into the mother. Then the Artist thinks, "Now I have lost," for he has lost heaven and sees nothing, and does not consider that a Virgin has been born anew. But he should have patience; what is impossible for the artist is possible for Nature. After the night, it becomes day; when the Tempter has finished all his temptations, the sign of the angels appears, and the devil who tempted him must retreat.

65. The Artist should well note this and dismiss the devil, laying the youth with his virginal heart in his bed and letting him eat his former food. Thus, fire is of two kinds, and light is also of two kinds: namely, a cold fire from the **Impression** <note>The "compression" or contracting force that Böhme identifies as the first property of nature, associated with Saturn.</note>, and a hot fire from the **Wheel of Mercury** <note>Mercury represents the force of motion, vibration, and communication within nature.</note> in **Sulfur** <note>Sulphur here refers to the "soul" or combustible substance of nature.</note>, as well as a cold light from the cold fire, and a warming light from the hot fire.

2. The cold light is false, and the hot is good; not that it is false in its own quality, but rather in the **Impression** within the cold **Sulfur**, it becomes a false desire in the sharpness of the **Fierceness**, like a false love that runs against gentleness. For its desire is **Saturn** and **Mars** <note>Saturn represents contraction and darkness; Mars represents the fire of energy and conflict.</note>: it carries its "sun" out into **Mars**, by which its shine of life is understood. And the warming light, which also receives its fire-sharpness in the **Impression**, in the **Sulfur** from **Mars**, carries its desire back into **Freedom** <note>The "Unground" or the divine realm beyond the struggle of nature.</note>, as if through dying in the fire, through the anguish; in the dying of the fire, it yields itself entirely free and abandons the quality of the **Fierceness**. Thus it is a common delight and nothing of its own, just as the sun gives its shine to all in common.

3. The sun’s shine is neither hot nor cold; only **Mercury** in the spirit of the great world creates a heat within it, in the quality of **Mars** and **Saturn**. For the sun ignites its desire, from which it becomes so hungry, desiring, and qualifying <note>The original German "qualificirend" ends mid-sentence here, with the catchword "cirend" expected on the next page.</note>

This is clearly seen in the person of **Christ**: He loved them, and did all good things for them, and healed them of their plagues; but because He did not spring from their fierce power—because He said He came from above and was the Son of GOD—this did not taste well to that cold, hot Fire-Power, for He wished to rule over them with Love.

But because no death can exist within it, Love sinks into the Fire-Terror and gives itself up in its desire, abandoning its own essence so that, in its desire, it stands according to its quality within the Death-Terror. ...of death shed his heavenly blood, and left it in death; thus the **Fierceness of God** <note>original: "Grimm GOttes"; referring to the harsh, wrathful foundation of nature that must be overcome.</note> was compelled to retain the heavenly **Love-Essence** <note>original: "Liebe-Wesen"; the substantial reality of divine love.</note> within itself. He wished to make Heaven out of the human earth, turning the four elements into only **One** in a single desire, and transforming the Fierceness of God within the human property into love.

8. Now, His wrath was a power of fire and fierceness, and it was enflamed within man. To resist this and transform it into a love required an earnest intensity; Love had to enter into the Wrath and surrender itself entirely to that Fierceness. It would not have sufficed for God to remain in Heaven and merely look upon humanity with love. It was impossible for the Wrath and Fierceness to have surrendered their power and yielded themselves into love by that alone; just as fire is not made better by light—it retains its fierceness for itself. But when a gentle essence enters the fire, such as water, then the fire is extinguished.

9. For water alone would not have done it; fire does not burn in water, but rather in the gentle **oily** <note>original: "olitätische"; referring to the spiritual "oil" or fuel that allows the light of love to burn without being consumed by the wrath of fire.</note>

### XIV. Of the Birth Chapter 11.

...transmutes, as if from **Venus** into **Sol** <note>original: "aus Venere in Solem"; from the planet/metal Venus (representing love/desire) into the Sun (representing divine light/gold).</note>; when the **Fire-Desire** enters into the **Water-Desire**, a gleam or radiance arises out of and within the water. For Venus is white and the Fire-Desire is red; now it transmutates itself into one color, which is yellow—that is, white and red together in one color. This is the majestic color. For when **Mercury** <note>In Böhme's thought, Mercury is the restless, driving force of life.</note> is transmuted into the power of joys, then the **Multiplication** <term>In alchemy, "multiplication" refers to the process of increasing the power of the philosopher's stone; here, it signifies the expansion of divine grace within the soul.</term> begins. He transmutes his mother, in whom he lay enclosed in death, into **Sol** (the Sun); He makes everything earthly into something heavenly, into a quality like that which the **Virgin** possessed. For here, the Virgin also loses her name, for she has given her love and her pearl to the **Knight**. Here, he is now called the **White Lion**, as the Scripture says regarding the Lion from the house of Israel and David, **Revelation 5:5**, who was to break the kingdom of the devil and destroy hell—that is, to break the **Wrath of God** and transform it into **Love**.

44. This Knight or Lion is neither man nor woman, but he is both; the **Fire-Tincture** and the **Light-Tincture** must become one, as the essence—which is **Venus**—and the spirit—which is **Mars** within **Mercury**. The Father’s love and wrath must be only one thing, then that same thing is called the **Kingdom of Joy**. As long as it is divided, there is only anxiety and torment in that thing, and mere desire; but when it burns in one single will, then it is a "Joy-Proceeding" out of itself. And this proceeding quality is called the **Holy Spirit**, as the life of the Godhead. Therefore, know why the blood of the **Virgin** and the **Youth** had to be shed together: so that the **Fire-Lion**, which had become manifest in the human quality, might die; so that the love of the Virgin might transmute his grimness <note>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, wrathful nature of the soul when separated from God's light.</note> into her quality within her love-blood, and so that she might receive the soul from the Youth. For in **Adam**, the Virgin faded away, because the soul departed from her will of love and from **Yieldedness** <term>original: "Gelassenheit"; a core concept in German mysticism referring to the total surrender of the self-will to God's will.</term> into a **Selfhood** <term>original: "Eignes"; the state of being centered on the ego.</term>, and became disobedient to God.

# Chapter 11: And the Signification of All Beings <note>The OCR reads "Cap. II," but the content and title "Bezeichnung aller Wesen" (Signification of All Beings) identify this as Chapter 11 of Jacob Böhme’s *Signatura Rerum*.</note>

80. [Adam] was not just woman, but both; he stood for forty days in Paradise without wavering. And when he fell, he remained until the third day—that is, forty hours in sleep—until God built the woman out of him.

81. Likewise, Israel had to be tested for forty days on Mount Sinai to see if they would live in obedience to God amidst wonders and deeds. When that could not be, God gave them the Law of His Covenant as a mirror of what had been promised in the Covenant. Thus the testing of the body lasted forty years over them, so that the body had to eat <term>Manna</term> <note>The miraculous bread provided by God to the Israelites in the desert, symbolizing spiritual nourishment.</note> to see if the human could be helped. When the body also could not endure, <term>Joshua</term> <note>The successor to Moses who led the Israelites into the Promised Land; Böhme views him as a precursor to Christ.</note> led them through the water with the Covenant of the Mirror. There, Israel had to maintain the Covenant in the mirror of the ultimate fulfillment through sacrifices, until the time of restoration arrived. Thus the <term>Knight of the Struggle</term> <note>original: *Ritter des Streits*. Böhme’s term for Christ as the heroic warrior who battles the forces of darkness and temptation.</note> stood forty days in the wilderness under temptation and endured the first state of Adam in Paradise. And the three hours of darkness on the Cross are the three hours of Christ’s temptation, just as the Devil tempted Him.

82. Furthermore, the forty hours in Christ's grave are the forty days of Adam in Paradise; and the forty days of Moses on the mountain, and the forty years in the wilderness; and the forty days after the Resurrection before the Ascension are the very same. Now that the Knight had endured Adam’s trial, the soul in its human property was also tested for forty days, to see if it would now eat of the Word of God and live in complete, <term>yielded obedience</term> <note>original: *gelassenem Gehorsam*. Refers to the central Böhmean concept of *Gelassenheit*, a state of surrendering one's own will to the Divine Will.</note> within the Will of God, being a true likeness and image of the Divine Power in the bottomless eternity, according to the <term>Trinity</term> <note>original: *Dreyheit*. The threefold nature of God, which Böhme believes is mirrored in the structure of the soul and the universe.</note> of the Godhead.

83. Likewise, the <term>Philosopher</term> <note>original: *Philosophus*. In this context, an Alchemist or seeker of the hidden wisdom of nature.</note> should also note that the essence of time exists in such a property. # XIV. On the Birth, Chapter II.

...mother of all beings, as in the Great Mystery <note>original: *Mysterio Magno*; in Böhme's thought, the "Mysterium Magnum" is the chaos or potentiality from which all things are expressed</note>, as in the soul of the macrocosm <note>original: *grossen Welt*</note>.

### Chapter 11. and the Designation of all Beings.

...property <note>The "property" refers to the self-willed, individual nature of the fallen soul that separates itself from God</note> had entered into the image of the Divine Essence and had swallowed the image of God within itself. Now the image in the creature of the souls cried out: *My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?* <note>original: "Mein GOtt, warum hast du mich verlassen?"; Christ’s cry from the cross is here interpreted as the cry of the human soul-image seeking restoration</note> For the human image, which faded in Adam and became alive again in Christ’s incarnation <note>original: *Menschwerdung*</note>, was meant to crush the head of God’s wrath in the fire-souls and transform its fire-power into the sun. So it now left the speaking Word of God; it fell into its soul's wrath, and there it felt God’s anger. For the speaking Word led it thus through anger into death, and out of dying into the solar life (understand this as the eternal Sun). Just as the candle dies in the fire, and from that same dying the light and the power go forth as the great, impassive life <note>original: *unfühlende Leben*; Böhme refers to a life that has transcended the painful "feelings" of the self-willed ego</note>; thus, from Christ’s dying, from His death, the eternal Divine Sun was meant and had to rise in human property.

88. But the selfhood of human property—the soul’s own will to live in fire-power—had to die here and drown in the image of love. The image of love also had to surrender itself to the wrath of dying, so that everything might fall into death, and in God’s will and mercy rise through death into the Paradise-quality <note>original: *Paradeis-Qual*; "Qual" here refers to the source-quality or essential vibration of Paradise</note>, in yieldedness <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a central concept in German mysticism meaning total resignation or surrendering of the self-will to God</note>, so that God’s Spirit alone may be all in all. Hell’s eye had to see through love, just as the light shines out of the fire, and the fire out of the darkness, and the darkness takes its origin <note>original: *Urstand*</note> from eternal desire.

89. And as Adam transformed God’s likeness into a dark form of death, so God transformed the likeness out of death back into light through His fire-wrath. He drew the likeness out of death again, just as a flower grows out of the wild earth.

90. Thus also in the philosophical work <note>The "philosophical work" refers to Alchemy, specifically the creation of the Philosopher’s Stone, which Böhme sees as a physical parallel to spiritual salvation</note>, Venus is forsaken when she takes the three wrathful properties into herself in wrath. Her wrath, as death, swallows her life; because of this, she loses her color. However, she also becomes a death to the three forms in wrath, for with love she drowns death. Thus life becomes a death to death (the wrath), and both now lie in the will of eternal nature, as in the Word of Creation <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*; the divine command "Let there be"</note>. This Word goes out with them on the Divine path, in the same manner as it had entered into being at the beginning of creation.

# XIV. On the Birth Chapter 11.

91. In the beginning, Paradise was manifest as the Universal <note>The "Universal" refers to the original, unified state of all things before they were divided by the fall or "wrath."</note>, and love shone through death or wrath. Thus it must become so again, that Venus <note>In Böhme’s system, Venus represents the power of love and the "water of life."</note> becomes the eye or the vision within the Fierceness; then out of Saturn, Mars, and Mercury, a Jupiter is formed; Mars becomes the Sun, and Saturn becomes the Moon. Thus Mars shines with the Sun out of Saturn into the Moon from the eye of Venus, and all seven are but One. Then the conflict has an end, and all is accomplished, until the resurrection of life.

92. And when Jesus had drunk the cup and said: *My God, why have you forsaken me?* <note>original: "Mein GOtt, warum hast du mich verlassen?"; Matthew 27:46</note>, he then said: *It is finished* <note>original: "Es ist vollbracht"; John 19:30</note>. Understand this as the work of human redemption. And he spoke further: *Father, into your hands I commend my spirit* <note>original: "Vater, ich befehle dir meinen Geist in deine Hände"</note>, and he bowed his head and passed away. Here now, the entire life of Christ surrendered itself into the Father's Desire, as into the will of eternal nature. He surrendered the will of his I-hood <note>original: "Ichheit"; the sense of "I-ness" or the individual ego</note>, as the creaturely will, entirely back into the Center—into the First Mother from which the soul-creature was born—as into the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium"; the "Mysterium Magnum" or the chaos/void from which God brings forth creation</note> of eternity. The will of Selfhood <note>original: "Selbheit"</note> had to re-enter entirely at the end of nature, so that Selfhood might die away completely, in order that God's eternal (single) Will and Spirit might be and do everything in humanity, alone and in all, and the creature thereafter might only be His instrument, in which He alone does what He wills.

93. Thus God the Father took our I-hood <note>original: "Ichheit"</note> back into His will through Christ’s death and entry. And so that this could be, He first tinctured <note>original: "tingirete"; an alchemical term meaning to transform or imbue a substance with a higher quality</note> humanity with the Divinity, so that humanity might be a lovely fragrance and sacrifice to Him in His power; for previously, death stood in the way.

94. Here Love broke death apart and unlocked the firm seal, so that the will could once again enter into that which it had been before it became a creature.

95. And thus we must all follow Him on His opened path; no one may see God unless God first becomes human in them, which occurs in the desire of faith. And then the corrupted will—which is caught in the death and wrath of God, and which blossoms in earthly essence and brings fruit unto death—must die away completely and fall into the free Serenity <note>original: "Gelassenheit"; a central term for Böhme meaning a state of yieldedness, surrender, or "letting go" of the self-will to God's will</note> in God's will and mercy.

Chapter 12. and the designation of all beings. 165

96. Then the individual will is with and in Christ at nature's end in the Great Mystery of God <note>The "Great Mystery" (*Mysterium Magnum*) is Böhme’s term for the source of all things, the chaotic potential out of which God's will creates existence.</note>, as if in God's hands: God's hands are the eternal desire, or the eternal will, which is unchangeable. Thus the will of the creaturely selfhood <note>original: "Selbheit"; the individual ego or the sense of "me and mine" that separates the soul from God.</note> dies; it goes entirely into Nothingness, so that it may no longer live for itself, but for God.

97. So it also happens in the Philosophical Work <note>Böhme uses "Philosophical Work" to refer to Alchemy, seeing the purification of metals as a direct map for the purification of the human soul.</note>: when the artist has previously seen great wonders, which the creaturely and natural will has worked in the power of Venus <note>In this system, Venus represents the power of love, beauty, and the "water" of life.</note>, and when he thinks he is close to the goal, then nature first dies for him in his work, and it becomes a dark night for him; the properties and power of every form must surrender themselves from their Center <note>original: "Centro"; the internal point of origin for any being or substance.</note>, and fall at nature's end; everything gives itself up freely, as a dead being; there is no further progress there, and everything divides in the Crown, as if into a thousand numbers.

98. Thus it is then again in the Mystery, at nature's end, as it was before it entered into the creature; understand that the essential desire, as the expressed Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"; Mercury represents the "vibration" or the active, speaking power of the Word in nature.</note>, must likewise go back to the end of its selfhood and surrender itself into the speaking Word.

99. The bodily being remains standing in the center of the four elements until the judgment of God, which now stands in death in the Center of the Sun <note>original: "Centro Solis"</note>, as if in the compaction <note>original: "Compaction"; a dense joining or thickening of spiritual substances.</note> of Venus and Mercury; which compaction in death falls entirely into one, as in a power of Jupiter <note>original: "Jovis"; Jupiter represents the light of wisdom and the "friendly" spiritual planet.</note>, as into the center of freedom.

100. For here the desire for cold and heat is extinguished; all earthly will and desire of the properties die away, and there is no more hunger for earthly or deathly properties.

Instead, it lived for the nature of the eternal Father in the seething of the pure Divine element: the life of the outer world died.

Had **GOD** not placed the sun into it—as a "Nature-God" of the outer visible world, which tinctures every working life and everything that grows and moves—then everything would exist in the dark <term>impression of death</term> <note>original: "Todes-Impression"</note>, as if in the abyss of hell.

Then, in the <term>Center of Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus</term>, the quality of the Sun rises in all seven forms; that is, in the <term>Word "Let there be"</term>, just like a new creation. ## A Short Summary of the Philosophical Work.

29. Our meaning might seem quite difficult to the reader, as we proceed so extensively and point to Christ within it; no one should wonder at this, for we do not seek gold or temporal goods through it, nor do we drive man into useless curiosity: We speak only with the children whom God has chosen for this, for the time is born when that which was lost shall be found again; and not only the *Universal* <note>original: "Universal"; in alchemy, the "Universal Medicine" or Stone that can heal both the physical body and the soul.</note> for the body of this world, but also for the soul.

30. The *Process* <note>original: "Proceß"</note> is very short in both cases and consists of only one quality, which is this: The tree is divided into seven forms (understand this as life). Now, the curse of God has entered into the seven forms; thus they are in conflict and against one another, and each form afflicts the other, and they can never become one unless all seven enter into death and die to their own will.

31. Now, this cannot happen unless a death comes into them which breaks the will of them all and is a death to them, just as the Godhead in Christ was a death to the human selfhood and the seven forms in human life, and yet had come to them for life: Thus it is here also; the human will in Christ was transformed into the eternal Sun, as into the *resignation* <note>original: "Gelassenheit"; a key concept in German mysticism meaning a total surrender or letting-go of the self-will to God.</note> in God. Thus, in the Philosophical Work, all forms must be transformed into one, as into the *Sun* <note>original: "Sol"; the alchemical name for gold and the symbol of spiritual perfection.</note>; out of seven, one must emerge, and yet it remains in seven, but in one desire, where every form desires the other in love; then there is no more conflict.

32. Therefore, let the *Artist* consider only how he may give death to death with the pure life, and how he may awaken the dead and faded life—which is heavenly, and stands imprisoned and hidden in the curse of God—so that it may take the *Fire-Soul* <note>original: "Feuer-Seele"; the energetic, passionate, or "sulfurous" aspect of the soul that requires purification.</note> back into itself; if he only brings it that far, then it has its own making within itself.

33. There is also no other possibility; the heavenly image—made according to God’s likeness in man—could not be helped after the fire-soul entered into its own selfhood <note>original: "Selbheit"; the state of being turned inward toward the ego and away from God.</note>, unless God’s Spirit led itself into the faded image, as into the heavenly essence, and surrendered itself—along with that image awakened in Him—into the soul-fire, as into the fierceness of death. In doing so, He would become a death to death, and to the fierce wrath of God, so that this wrath might be drowned in love, in the blood of the heavenly essence. And although there could be no separation, nor any dying, it was nonetheless a dying of the wrath, so that the wrath might be transformed into joy and love.

34. In the same way, the <term>Artist’s</term> <term>Work</term> <note>original: "Artisten Werck"; the alchemical process of transmuting base matter into a divine or "universal" substance.</note> is absolutely nothing else; for man was created out of all beings, from heaven and earth. But when he became entirely earthly, and the curse came upon him, so too did the curse come upon the earthly essence from which man was made. Thus, heaven was closed to man, and heaven was also closed within the earth—in metals, trees, and herbs—within man’s food, and within all that belonged to his adornment and delight.

35. The soul of the earth, as the property from the fire of the first <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principii"; the first of Böhme's three realms, representing the dark, fiery power and divine wrath that underlies existence.</note>, has entered into its own selfhood, as into God's wrath. Now, heaven stands hidden within it; therefore, the <term>Artist</term> <note>original: "Artista"; the practitioner of alchemy or spiritual transformation.</note> must, in his <term>work</term>, bring the soul in the curse and the heaven back into one. He must lead the soul back into heaven, otherwise there is no possibility. Since he cannot bring the soul in its wickedness into heaven—for it does not want to go—he must instead lead heaven into the soul, and surrender heaven entirely, so that the soul may eat of heaven, whether it wants to or not. Thus, heaven must become as if dead within the soul, so that the soul cannot get rid of it, no matter how violently it rages against it, until it stirs within its own fierceness and enters with desire into heaven, as into the faded essence. It seeks to murder that essence, just as the Jews did to Christ; and when it thus enters with its desire into the faded image, as into the heavenly essence, the image of the heavenly essence falls into the murderer's jaws. Thus, the heavenly essence gives its desire into the murderer, and the murderer is terrified before the Love-

There he may grasp the spirit of the **Universal**; otherwise, it is all in vain. We wish to warn the over-curious not to just stare at this; they will achieve nothing at all on this path unless they step into it themselves. Then it will become manifest to them without much searching, for the way is childlike <note>simple, requiring the humble faith of a child</note>.

# XIV. Concerning the Birth. Chapter 13. #

...embodiment <note>The catchword "Ver-" from the previous page completes the word "Verkörperung" or "embodiment."</note> in the tangible and visible. Among the seven <term>forms of nature</term> <note>These are the seven fundamental qualities or "Source-Spirits" in Böhme's cosmology that govern all existence.</note>, one form is always the highest; the others depend upon it and provide their accompanying signs according to how strong each is in its <term>essence</term> <note>The essential being or inner substance of a thing.</note>. And just as these forms stand in their specific order within every thing, so they give shape to the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>—every thing and creature according to its kind. This is the manifestation of Divine Wisdom in the spoken **Word**, arising out of love and wrath.

2. No thing exists that does not have its soul within it according to its specific property, and the soul is a grain for another body. Everything that lives and grows has its seed within itself; God has enclosed all things in His **Word** and expressed them into a form, just as the will has enclosed itself in desire. That which is **Spoken** is a model of the **Speaker** and, in turn, contains the power of speaking within itself; this same speaking is a seed for another image modeled after the first: for both are active, the Speaker and the Spoken.

3. The Speaker exists within Himself as if in eternity, and the Spoken also exists within itself, as if in time. The Speaker is the **Master**, and the Spoken is the **instrument**. The Speaker produces the nature of eternity, and the Spoken produces the nature of time. Each, in its own manifestation, creates two properties, such as light and darkness; within these stands the <term>element of all beings</term>, which in the Spoken divides into four elements, but in the Speaker is only One.

4. The element in itself is neither hot nor cold, nor dry nor wet, but is a **delight** <note>original: "Lust"; in Böhme’s writing, this refers to a joyful, divine inclination or the "pleasure" God takes in manifestation.</note>, like a desiring will, within which Divine Wisdom creates the colors of distinction. All this occurs according to the property of desire, in which there is neither number nor end; only in the four elements is there number and end. ### Chapter 13. and the Designation of All Beings. ###

->M 2<-

**Understanding** comes alone from God, for it originates <note>original: "urständet." A term used by Böhme to describe something taking its original "stand" or arising from its primal source.</note> out of eternal nature.

6. All life that has its goal in the **spoken Word** stands in <term>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</term> <note>original: "Sale, Sulphure und Mercurio." We will represent from where **Evil** and **Good** originate, and how they originate, to give the person of understanding a reason to seek; and we will show how the will toward Evil and Good originates, how Evil is the death of Good, and conversely, how Good is the death of Evil.

...the **Impression** <note>original: "Impression." Thus, within the fire, a struggle remains between the cold and the heat: the cold wishes to maintain its life according to its own property, and as it moves toward life, it ignites the heat within itself through the Impression. Then, the heat takes power away from the cold and consumes the cold's essence. Consequently, the **Fire-Spirit** cannot subsist either, for without essence it is extinguished; it must therefore constantly and without ceasing "die" within itself, in the fire-anguish-desire. As long as it has the cold's essence to consume, its life rises up, and yet it is nothing but a constant dying and consuming. In its consumability lies the greatest hunger for essence. This hunger passes through and with the consumability out of the dying of the fire, exiting itself to dwell in the **Nothing**. Yet it cannot remain in the Nothing, nor can it be a nothing; therefore, the fire pulls it back into itself, for its desire stands toward its mother. The fire constantly pulls it back into itself, and this is the life of the fire. This is the spirit which, while in the fire, is rightly called **Wind** because of its strength, and once it has gone out, is rightly called **Air** because of the life of its gentleness.

### Chapter 13. and the Description of All Beings.

...into the **Nothing** <note>original: "Nichts." 19. It is a tester and knower of all properties, for it was born through them all and has proceeded from them all. In Böhme’s theology, the "wrath" of the Father is the raw, consuming fire of divine power that must be softened by the "Love" of the Son to become merciful.</note>, whereby the Father becomes merciful; so also does it occur in the **spoken Word** <note>original: "ausgesprochenem Wort." 36. Not that one should or could drive out and kill the cold poison of Mercury with enkindled heat; no, if the cold poison is enkindled, then the medicine must be of the same nature; but it must first be liberated from the cold—as from the enkindled cold **grimness** <term>grimness: (German: *Grimme*) A state of harsh, unmediated, or destructive intensity in nature.</term>—and placed into **gentleness** <note>original: "Sanftmuth." 37. 38. Therefore, if life is to stand in its own right, heat and cold must stand in equal essence, so that they harmonize with one another, and no enmity or deviation exists in either; neither must surpass the other, but they must stand in **One Will**.

39. For the enkindled cold desires no heat, but only equality; every hunger desires equality for its food. But if the hunger were too intensely enkindled in cold, one does not give it a cure that is likewise enkindled [in wrath]; it should indeed be of the same high degree of cold, but its **violence** <note>original: "Gewalt." The raw, aggressive power of a natural force before it is harmonized.</note> must first be taken from it, so that it is only like the mother who brings it forth—not according to the enkindled poisonous quality, but according to the mother’s joy. Thus the illness, as the poison in anxiety, will be transformed into such joy.

40. Thus life takes its first property upon itself again. It is not the rough body in opposition that belongs to the **Cure** <term>Cure: (Latin: *Cura*) The process of healing or medical treatment.</term>, but its **Oil** <note>In alchemy, the "Oil" is the balsamic, life-preserving essence within a substance that holds the spiritual light-principle.</note>; that must be softened with its own love—understand this as a gentle essence that also belongs to that same property. For the **seven forms of nature** <note>Böhme’s system of seven qualities (such as contraction, expansion, and rotation) that describe all manifestation.</note> are only One in the **Center**, so one must lead that same oil so far in the wheel...

Referring to a substance of the same nature that has been harmonized, acting as a restorative "like-to-like" remedy.</note> of its being for support, it remains in faintness, and then the enkindled grimness consumes itself and also falls into faintness; thus natural death is in both, and the weaving life in the body ceases. But if it receives the likeness again, it strengthens itself once more, and so the enkindled hunger of the illness must cease.

This is so that the same likeness does not **operate** <term>operate: (German: *qualificire*) To act, feel, or produce effects through specific qualities or properties.</term> in either heat or cold, but in its own love-desire, as in its best taste; thus it will also lead the heat in the body into such a desire. All decay in the body comes from the cold: when **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: In Böhme's system, the "mother" or foundational substance that contains the potential for both the dark fire and the light.</term> is too greatly enkindled by heat, the right and property of the cold dies away and enters into mourning.

43. **Mercury** <term>Mercury: (Latin: *Mercurius*) The vital, moving spirit or "workman" of nature that drives all movement, perception, and life.</term> is the moving life in all things, and his mother is Sulphur; thus life and death lie in Sulphur, as in the struggling mercurial wheel. In Sulphur there is fire, light, and darkness; the **compression** <term>compression: (Latin: *Impression*) The contracting force of nature that draws inward, creating density, darkness, and "matter."</term> gives darkness, cold, and hardness, as well as great anxiety; and from the compression of the drawing-inward arises Mercury; he is the **sting** <note>original: *Stachel*. The prick or goad of restless energy that forces movement out of the stillness of the dark.</note> of the drawing-inward, as the mobility or restlessness, and arises in the great anxiety of the compression. Because cold arises in the compression—as a dark, cold fire due to the hardness—and a hot fire arises in the sting of anxiety—as in the restlessness—Mercury is the wheel of movement and an awakening of cold and heat. At this point, it is only a painful torment in heat and cold, as a cold and hot **poison-anxiety** <note>original: *Gift-Angst*. The corrosive, agonizing state of natural forces before they are harmonized by the light of divine love.</note>, driving like a wheel; yet it is the cause of joy and all life and movement: but if it is to be redeemed from the anxiety and led into joy, it must be led through death.

### XIV. Of the Birth. Chapter 13.

44. Thus every disease and pain is a **death-property**, for **Mercury** <term>Mercury: (German: *Mercurius*) In Böhme's system, this is the active, mobile spirit or "wheel" of nature that drives all movement and perception.</term> has ignited and burnt itself too much either in heat or cold. Through this, the substance or flesh—which Mercury has drawn to itself in its desire, as if from its mother in **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: Representing the substantial "womb" or the dark, fiery core of a thing's being from which Mercury emerges.</term>—has been burnt. From this arises "earthliness" <note>original: *Irdigkeit*. The state of being heavy, gross, or material rather than spiritual.</note>, both in the water and the flesh. Just as the matter of the earth and the stones—being the coarseness of the same—is nothing other than a burnt Sulphur and water in the property of Mercury, where the **Salniter** <term>Salniter: A term Böhme uses for a kind of cosmic gunpowder or vital, explosive potential within the "wheel" of nature.</term> was burnt in the **clash** <note>original: *Schrack*. A sudden shock, crack, or terrifying flash that occurs when nature's forces collide.</note> of the Mercurial wheel, from which the manifold salts arise; from this comes the stench and the foul taste.

45. Otherwise, if Mercury operated therein in the **Oil of Sulphur** <note>The "Oil of Sulphur" represents a state of balance where the harsh fire is tempered into a gentle, nourishing light.</note>, so that it might be led through the death of the **impression** <term>impression: (German: *Impression*) The "drawing-in" or contracting force of nature that hardens spirit into matter.</term> of heat and cold, then the Earth would be a Paradise again, and the desire for joy would green and bloom once more through the anguish of the impression of cold.

46. This is why God has cursed the Earth; for the "good" was withdrawn from the Mercurial wheel. This good is the **love-desire**, which arises in the eternal freedom and reveals itself with this Mercurial wheel through cold and heat, and goes out through the fire and makes a shine of light. The curse was led into it, which is a fleeing of the love-desire.

47. So now this Mercury stands as a life in the Sulphur of its mother, presently under the curse, existing in the anguish of heat and cold. In its "clash" or **Salnitric boiling** <note>original: *Salnitrischen Sude*. A seething, chemical-like agitation of the inner life-forces.</note>, it continually creates **Salt** according to whatever property is ignited in each place and in each body. These same salts are then the "taste" within the seven properties of nature.

48. If Mercury is now ignited too much in the cold, it creates in the Salnitric clash within its mother, the Sulphur, a cold, hard, impressing salt. From this, **Melancholy**, darkness, and sadness arise in the life of the Sulphur. For whatever kind of salt is in a thing, such a luster of fire and such a shine of life from the fire is also within it.

49. But if Mercury is ignited in excessive heat, it burns the essence of the cold and creates raging and stinging, according to the impression and according to the property of the "sting." From this, great heat arises in the Sulphur; and as the water is dried up and consumed, then the hunger of the desire has—

57. But if it is to ascend higher, it must take on another property; then it is no longer in its own degree, and no longer possesses its own virtue, but a foreign one. 58. Thus, its own virtue—following its better part—is led upward into the "regiment" or governing state. In this way, it is powerful enough in its likeness to meet all sicknesses without any other interference. For the origin of life desires no multiplicity, but only its own likeness, so that it may stand, live, and burn in its own power.

59. But with the curse, the **Turba** <term>Turba: (Latin: "turmoil" or "disturbance") The destructive element or "awakened wrath" that disrupts the natural order and leads to decay.</term> was introduced, so that the properties now stand in the strife of Mercury <term>Mercury: (Latin: *Mercurii*) The active, moving principle in nature that can produce either life or poison depending on its state.</term>. Yet in every property, in every herb, or whatever it may be that grows or arises from the seething of the four elements, there is also a hidden fire. For all things that are in the four elements have their origin in the eternal (single) element, in which there is no strife, neither heat nor cold, but a balanced weight of all properties in a "Love-Play," just as it is in **Paradise**; and that same element flourished through the earth in the beginning of this world before the curse.

60. So it is also still hidden in all things, and may yet be opened through understanding and art, so that the original virtue overcomes the ignited malice. Although we humans may not have the full authority to proceed by our own power, it nonetheless happens by God’s permission, He who has turned His mercy back toward us and has reopened Paradise and its concept within man.

61. If God has given us power to become His children and to rule over the world, why not also over the curse of the earth? No one should consider it impossible; it requires only a **Divine Understanding** and knowledge. This shall flourish in the **Time of the Lilies** <note>Time of the Lilies: A prophetic period of spiritual peace and enlightenment expected by Böhme and his followers, contrasting with the "Babel" of religious conflict.</note>, and not in **Babel** <note>Babel: A term used by Böhme to describe the "confusion" of organized, dogmatic churches and worldly scholarship.</note>, to whom we have written nothing.

# ->XIV. Of the Birth Chapter 14.<-

...go, so that your understanding may be opened in practical ways <note>original: "Handgriffen" — literally "hand-grips," implying a tangible or manual grasp of these spiritual mysteries.</note>, lest I wander off: I write solely in the spirit of vision, how the birth of both good and evil occurs, and I open the well; he whom God has appointed for it shall draw the water; here I will only describe the wheel of life <note>original: "Rad des Lebens" — a recurring concept in Böhme’s work representing the dynamic, revolving cycle of natural and divine forces.</note> as it is in itself.

2. Now when I speak of **Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt**, I am speaking of a single thing, whether it be spiritual or corporeal; all created things are that one single thing, but the properties in the birth of this one thing provide the distinctions. For whether I name a human, or a lion, bear, wolf, hare, or other animal, as well as a root, herb, wood, or whatever it might be, it is still the same single thing.

3. Everything that is corporeal is the same essence; the herbs and trees as well as the living creatures: but each in its distinction of the first beginning, as the property has imprinted itself in each thing through the **Word Fiat** <note>original: "Verbo Fiat" — the creative "Let there be" spoken by God at the beginning of the world.</note>. Thus also is the same kind in its propagation, and everything stands in seed and rebirth; and there is no thing that does not have something **Fixed** <term>Fixed: In alchemy, the "fixed" (fixum) is the stable, permanent part of a substance that resists the fire, representing the eternal soul or essence.</term> within itself, whether hidden or manifest, for everything shall exist for the glory of God.

4. Whatever has originated <note>original: "geurständet" — a word Böhme coined to describe something taking its primal rise or "original standing" from a source.</note> from the eternal **Fixed**, such as angels and human souls, these remain in their fixed essence, unbreakable. But whatever has originated in the unfixed, such as with the movement of time, returns again into the first movement from which it took its origin, and is a model of the likeness it held here—much like a looking-glass, or an image in a mirror that is lifeless. For thus it was from eternity before the times of the world, which the Highest led into an image, into comprehensible, natural life in time, to behold the great wonders of His wisdom in a created being, as it stands before our eyes.

5. Fifthly, the **Free Will's** departure out of the darkness and out of the fire, to dwell within itself: there the free will has taken the brilliance unto itself, so that it illuminates and shines like a light out of the fire; and the powerful desire of the free will—which it sharpened in the fire, in that it died to the fire of the essence of darkness of the first form and that darkness was consumed—now draws into itself the essence from the fire-death, according to its hunger, into the desire of the light. This is now **Water**, and in the brilliance it is the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur: A spiritual-alchemical essence that gives color, life, and medicinal power to matter; the "bloom" of the divine light.</term> of fire and light, as a love-desire or a beauty of colors: and here all colors originate, as we have fully set forth in other books, especially in *The Threefold Life of Man*. Sixthly, the **Voice and Sound**, which in the first form is only a knocking or a resonance of the hardness, and died to the same in the fire; but in the fifth form, in the love-desire, it is again captured as an echo out of the death of the fire in the light’s brilliance within the Tincture, in a lovely quality; therein the five **senses** <note>original: "Sensus"</note>—namely hearing, seeing, feeling, smelling, and tasting—arise from the fire in the Tincture of the light. Seventhly, the **Menstruum** <note>original: "Menstruum" — in alchemy, the "universal solvent" or the nutritive maternal blood/fluid that forms the body of a thing.</note>

## Chapter 14 and the Designation of All Beings.

25. Now take good note of the nature and will of their opening <gloss>revelation or unfolding</gloss>, how nature is introduced into seven properties: For we do not speak of a beginning, since in eternity there is no beginning; rather, the **eternal birth** is from eternity to eternity within itself. This same eternal birth, according to the property of eternity—through its own desire and movement—has introduced itself into a time, with this visible world as a likeness of the eternal spirit, in such a creaturely form like a prototype of the Eternal. We will speak of this hereafter and show what the creature is: namely, a likeness of the eternal working, and how it also contains that same working within itself temporally.

26. Understand us then regarding the fire: the fire is the **principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note> of all life; it gives essence and **torment** <gloss>the quality of feeling or "qualification"</gloss> to the darkness. Otherwise, there would be no **perceptibility** <gloss>original: "Findlichkeit" — the ability of a being to find or experience itself</gloss> in the darkness, nor any spirit, but mere hardness and a hard, sharp, bitter, rough sting, as it truly is in the eternal darkness. But as far as the hot fire can be reached, the dark, stinging property stands in the ascending, desiring essence like a terrible madness, so that it may be known what wisdom and folly are. Thus the fire also gives torment and properties to the light, as the desire for freedom; however, understand this correctly:

27. Freedom, as the **Nothing** <note>Böhme refers here to the "Ungrund," the groundless void of God before manifestation.</note>, has no essence in itself; rather, the **impression** <gloss>the contracting or drawing-in force</gloss> of the strict desire makes the first essence. This is taken up by the will-spirit of freedom—which reveals itself through the nature of the desire—and leads it out through the fire, where the coarseness or roughness then dies away; understand it thus:

28. When the lightning-flash of the fire reaches the dark essence, it is a great **terror** <term>Schrack: a sudden, violent shock or "crack" (like thunder) that marks the transition from darkness to light</term>, from which the cold fire is startled and as if it dies; it becomes powerless and sinks beneath itself. This terror occurs in the kindling of the fire within the essence of **anguish** <note>original: "Angst" — Böhme's term for the agonizing tension or "narrowness" of the first three properties of nature.</note>.
