# XIV. Of the Birth Ch. 15.

...and aversion, from which anger arises as the **fire of breaking** <note>original: *Feuer der Zerbrechung*. In Böhme's thought, this refers to the destructive, fragmented energy that occurs when the soul's fire is separated from divine light.</note>.

12. All sins arise from **selfhood** <term>selfhood <gloss>original: *Selbheit*. The state of being trapped in one's own ego and selfish desires, separated from the divine.</gloss></term>, for selfhood swings itself with **desire** <term>desire <gloss>original: *Begierde*. A fundamental force in Böhme’s cosmos; it can be either a selfish craving or a holy longing.</gloss></term> into its own property; it turns itself into greed and envy, it draws foreign beings to itself in its self-desire, and also makes the owners of those foreign beings into enemies against itself, so that sin is worked with sin, and disgust with disgust, and everything runs into and under one another as a total abomination before the **eternal mother** <note>The "Eternal Mother" is Böhme’s term for the divine source or the "Great Mystery" (Mysterium Magnum) from which all things are born.</note>.

13. Thus we should think in the same way regarding the reborn will, which enters out of its **I-hood** <term>I-hood <gloss>original: *Ichheit*. The individualistic focus on the "I," synonymous with the selfish ego.</gloss></term> or selfhood back into **yieldedness** <term>yieldedness <gloss>original: *Gelassenheit*. The spiritual practice of surrendering one's personal ego and will to the divine will.</gloss></term>; it also becomes an enemy and a disgust to selfhood, just as sickness is an enemy to health, and health in turn is an enemy to sickness; thus the yielded will and the own-will are in constant enmity, a perpetual war and struggle.

14. The own-will seeks only what serves its selfhood: and the yielded will worries for nothing, but leads its desire solely and alone into its eternal mother, so that it may be at one with her; it wants to be "nothing," so that the mother alone may be "everything" in it. The own-will says to the yielded will: "You are foolish to give yourself over to death, when you could live magnificently in me"; but the yielded will says: "You are my disgust, pain, and aversion, and you lead me out of eternity into time, into nothing but sorrow and misery; you make me sick for a time, and then you give my body to the earth and my soul to hell."

15. Right and true yieldedness is the dying of the disgust against **GOD**: whoever entirely abandons their selfhood, and gives themselves with mind and desire, senses and will, into **GOD’S** mercy—into the dying of **JESUS CHRIST**—is dead to the earthly world in their will, and is a **twofold human** <term>twofold human <gloss>original: *zweyfacher Mensch*. The concept that a person exists simultaneously in two realms: an outer earthly self and an inner spiritual self.</gloss></term>, where the disgust works within itself only toward dying; but the yielded will lives in Christ's death, and rises up forever in Christ's resurrection in **GOD**. And though the own-desire sins—which indeed cannot do otherwise than sin—nevertheless the yielded will does not live in sin: for it has died to the desire for sin, and lives through Christ in **GOD**, in the land of the living.

It is back at the goal where it was before it became a creature, and in the will in which God created it; it is an **instrument** in the reverberance of God, upon which only God's will-spirit strikes, to His honor and wonder-work.

For it is not the delusion or one's own thoughts arising in the spoken resonance that is **God's** Word. It creates the form in the heart as a Divine desire, through which the soul's will is drawn into **God**.

### The 16th Chapter.

## Of the Eternal Signature and Heavenly Joy; Why All Things Have Been Introduced into Evil and Good?

### Summaries.

### Chapter 16. and the Signature of all Beings. <note>original: "Bezeichnung aller Wesen." In Böhme's philosophy, this refers to the 'Signature of All Things,' the idea that the internal essence of a thing is revealed through its outward form.</note>

Revelation manifests from eternity to eternity in two essences: as Evil and as Good. What is evil to one thing is good to another; Hell is evil to the angels, for they were not created within it, but for the other hellish creatures, it is good.

27. Likewise, Heaven is evil to hellish creatures, for it is their poison and death, an eternal dying and an eternal prison. Therefore, there is an eternal enmity, and God is called a "God" only according to the Light of His love. He is indeed everything Himself, but according to the Darkness He says: "I am a jealous, angry God, and a consuming fire." Every creature shall remain in its <term>place <gloss>original: "Loco."</gloss></term> wherein it was seized in its creation and formed into an image, and must not deviate from that <term>harmony <gloss>original: "Harmonye."</gloss></term>, or else it becomes an enemy to the Essence of all essences.

28. Thus, Hell is just as much an enemy to the Devil, for he is a foreign guest within it, like a perjurer cast out of Heaven. He wants to be a master in a place where he was not created. The whole of creation rebukes him as a perjured, fallen, false spirit who has stepped out of his proper order; for even Nature in its wrath is his enemy. Although he shares that same property <note>meaning the "wrathful" or "dark" quality of nature</note>, he is nonetheless a stranger who wants to be master, yet he has lost his kingdom and is merely a housemate in the wrath of God. He who was too rich has become too poor; he had everything when he stood in the Father’s property in humility, but now he has nothing and is moreover imprisoned in the abyss. This is his shame: that he is a king and yet gambled away his kingdom through pride. The royal creature remains, but the governance is gone; from a king, he has become an <term>executioner <gloss>original: "Nach-Richter." This literally means an "after-judge," a term for one who carries out a sentence.</gloss></term>. Wherever God’s wrath takes hold, there he is the judge, acting as a <term>steward <gloss>original: "Amtmann." An official or bailiff.</gloss></term> of God's wrath, who must nevertheless do what his Master wills.

Yes, dear Reason, now you think you have the prize <note>original: "den Braten," literally "the roast," an idiom meaning to think one has solved or won something</note>, but first learn your A-B-C’s in the Great <term>Mystery <gloss>original: "Mysterio."</gloss></term>.

# XIV. Of the Birth Chap. 16.

30. Everything that originates from the eternal Will, as from the great eternal <term>Mystery <gloss>original: "Mysterio." In this context, it refers to the hidden, unmanifested source of all potential existence.</gloss></term> of all beings (such as angels and the souls of men), stands in an equal balance between Evil and Good. They possess free will, just as God Himself does. Whichever desire within the creature arises into its <term>qualification <gloss>original: "Qualificirung." This refers to the specific energetic quality, temperament, or "flavor" that a being takes on.</gloss></term> and surpasses the other, that becomes the creature’s characteristic property. It is like a candle that gives birth to a fire from itself, and from the fire, the wind, which the wind the fire draws back into itself and yet gives out again. And when this spirit has gone forth from the fire and light, it is free from the fire and light: whichever quality it then takes up, that is what it is.

31. The first Mystery, wherein the creature stands, is the all-essential Mystery; the second, in the proceeding spirit, is the creature's own property and its own will. Since every angel has its own spirit, which is born out of its own mystery—which has its origin <note>original: "Urstand," meaning the primordial ground or source of being.</note> in eternity—why then does that same spirit become a tempter of God and test the Mystery? This testing captures it in the <term>Wrath <gloss>original: "Grimme." For Böhme, this is the harsh, fiery, and severe side of God's nature that becomes "Hell" when separated from His Love.</gloss></term>, as happened to Lucifer. He had within himself the pull toward both God’s wrath and God’s love; why then does the spirit (which is born from both and is the likeness of the Spirit of God) not remain in its seat in obedience, like a child before its mother in humility?

32. If you say, "he cannot," that is no valid reason. Every spirit stands in the place where it was created, in an equal balance, and has free will. It is one spirit with the all-essential eternal Spirit, and it may draw a delight for itself from the all-essential eternal Spirit however it chooses, whether in God’s love or in His anger. Whatever it directs its delight into, the essence and property of that it receives in the great Mystery of all beings. Since the birth <note>of existence</note> is manifest in God in both love and anger, why should it not also be so in the creature, who was created into an image out of God’s essence and will, out of His voice and <term>reverberation <gloss>original: "Halle." This suggests a divine sound or echo that brings form to the universe.</gloss></term>? Whichever quality of that resonance the creature awakens within itself, that same resonance echoes through and governs the creature.

# Chapter 16. and the Signification of all Beings.
<meta>catchword: being:</meta>

...captured by the property of the eternal Mystery. Now, Lucifer was indeed captured while in a good angelic property; this is proven enough by the fact that he was once an angel in heaven. But his own incorporeal Will-Spirit swung itself into the <term>fierce mother <gloss>original: "grimme Mutter." Yet the Will-Spirit is free; it is the <term>primordial source <gloss>original: "Urstand." This refers to the foundational origin or "standing place" of a being's existence.</gloss></term> in eternity; it does what it wills.

34. Because the Will-Spirit—which originates from both Love and <term>Wrath <gloss>original: "Zorn." Having risen out of a state of harmony into one of disharmony, the spirit had to be driven into its own likeness <note>Meaning, the spirit is forced to inhabit the state it chose for itself.</note>. This is his Fall, and such is also the fall of all wicked men.

35. Now, self-centered Reason cites the Scripture where it is written: *Many are called, but few are chosen.* <note>Matthew 22:14</note>. Likewise: *Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated!* And: *Does not a potter have power to make from one lump of clay whatever he wills?* <note>Romans 9:13, 21</note>. I also say that many of them are called, but few are chosen. For they do not *will* to be; they swing their free will into God’s Wrath. It is there they are captured, and thus they are then chosen as children of the Wrath. Yet, in Adam, they were all called into Paradise, and in Christ, they were all called into the <term>Rebirth <gloss>original: "Wiedergeburt." The spiritual process of returning to the divine image.</gloss></term>. But they would not; the free will would not. It swung itself into the fierceness of God, which captured it, and so they were not chosen children. For God’s Love chooses for itself only that which is like it, and so also does God’s Wrath. And yet, the Gate of Rebirth stands open even to the godless man whom the Wrath of God has captured: For man has "death" within him, through which he may die away from the evil. But the Devil does not have this "death" <note>Böhme suggests that because humans are mortal, they can "die" to their old nature and be reborn, whereas the Devil, being purely spiritual and "perfectly" formed in his initial state, remains fixed in his chosen fallen state.</note>, for he was created in the highest perfection.

The spiritual lineage or "thread" leading to the incarnation of Christ.</gloss></term> was swung upward in the <term>wrestling wheel <gloss>original: "ringenden Rade." This is Böhme's term for the dynamic, rotating forces of nature and spirit as they struggle toward manifestation.</gloss></term>, and in Esau was the Fall of Adam. Now, Christ was promised into humanity for this very reason: to heal the Fall of Adam, and to redeem the Esau who was captured in the Wrath.

# XIV. On the Birth, etc. Chapter 16. 244

It is a nearly bright portal of the great <term>Mystery <gloss>original: "Mysterii." This refers to the *Mysterium Magnum*, a central concept in Böhme’s thought describing the hidden, divine source from which all reality originates.</gloss></term> of all beings. No one shall grasp it in its own foundation through <term>glossing <gloss>original: "Glossiren." The act of adding scholarly commentaries or intellectual interpretations.</gloss></term> and one's own cleverness; but it may embrace the true seeker and bring much use and joy, and it shall also be helpful in all natural things, if one prepares oneself rightly for it and seeks in the fear of God: for this is the time of seeking.

48. For a <term>lily <gloss>In Böhme’s prophetic language, the "Lily" symbolizes a coming age of spiritual purity and the blossoming of true divine knowledge within the soul and across the world.</gloss></term> blooms over mountain and valley, in all ends of the earth: He who seeks there, finds.
->Amen.<-

## THE END

<image-desc>A large, elaborate calligraphic flourish or pen-work design consisting of symmetrical, interlocking loops and swirls, centered on the lower half of the page.</image-desc>

<summary>This concluding page of Chapter 16 serves as a final exhortation, identifying the text as a gateway to the "Great Mystery" and promising spiritual discovery to those who seek with true devotion. It famously mentions the blooming of the "Lily," a symbol of spiritual renewal that Böhme believed would spread across the earth.</summary>
